dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_base_shelter: If I ever need walls around me, where are yours?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_base_directi: Give me directions to your post?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_base_mark_ma: Mark my map — where's home for you?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_base_follow_: If I follow your cook-smoke, where do I end up?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_base_travele: Do any of your camps take travelers for the night?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_base_officer: Your command post — where do I find it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_stonewall_ca: Tell me where your camp is.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_stonewall_ga: How many of you are garrisoned near here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_stonewall_st: Where do you keep your stores?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_stonewall_ga: Which road leads to your gate?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_stonewall_po: Show me your positions on a map.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_stonewall_co: Where can I find your commander?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_stonewall_wa: Where does your water come from?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_stonewall_ba: Every fort has a back way in. Where's yours?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_stonewall_si: What do your signal fires mean?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_vague_land_h: Who holds this stretch of land?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_vague_lost: I'm a little lost. Where am I, exactly?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_vague_shelte: Where could a traveler shelter around here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_vague_trade_: Where do people trade in these parts?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_vague_river_: Does this road follow the river?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_vague_roof: How far to anything with a roof?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_vague_who_el: Who else is out here besides you?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_dug_in: Where are your enemies dug in?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_hurt_t: If I wanted to hurt your rivals, where would I start?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_steer_: Where should I steer clear of, enemy-wise?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_other_: You know where the other side camps?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_mark_e: Mark the enemy's position for me.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_scouts: What did your scouts find out there?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_neighb: Who's your nearest hostile neighbor, and where?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_same_h: I'm hunting the same people you are. Where do I look?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_news_t: I'll trade you news for news. Where's the enemy?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_watchf: Whose watchfires are those on the horizon?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rival_unfini: I have unfinished business with your rivals. Point me at them.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_officer_enem: You're an officer. Where do the enemy lines run?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_officer_brie: Give me the briefing you'd give your own scouts.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_officer_next: Where will the enemy press next?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_officer_camp: Share your campaign map with me.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_officer_real: Where does the real front run these days?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_officer_trou: Where's the enemy making trouble for you?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rivalref_at_: Who are you at war with?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rivalref_win: Which side is winning out here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rivalref_pay: I'd pay good coin for enemy positions.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rivalref_bat: Where did the last battle happen?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rivalref_spi: Do you have spies in the other camps?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rivalref_nex: When's your next raid, and where?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rivalref_fro: What's the latest from the front?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_rivalref_thi: Point me at your enemies and I'll thin them out for you.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_chang: When do your patrols change over?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_round: How often do your rounds pass this way?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_next_: When's the next patrol due through here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_shift: How long is a watch shift for you?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_after: Do your patrols keep walking after dark?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_route: What route do your patrols run?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_gap: Is there ever a gap between patrols?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_watch: Which roads do you watch closest?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_range: How far out do your patrols range?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_safe_: When's the safest hour to travel your roads?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrol_horn_: If I hear your horn, what does it mean?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrolref_sk: Which paths do your patrols skip?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrolref_se: How many sentries stand your wall?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrolref_al: How fast can you raise an alarm?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrolref_mi: Do you even watch the roads after midnight?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_patrolref_th: Your patrols look thin lately. Short-handed?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_road_stopped: Will I be stopped again if I keep walking this road?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_road_last_tr: When was the last trouble on this road?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_road_night_u: Does anyone use this road at night?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_road_carts: Do traders' carts still run this way?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_terrain_fore: What's in the forest beyond here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_terrain_ruin: I saw ruins to the east. Know anything about them?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_terrain_cave: Any caves worth knowing about nearby?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_terrain_smok: I saw smoke over the hills. Yours?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_terrain_swam: Is there a way around the swamp?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_terrain_coas: How far to the coast from here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_terrain_bite: Anything out here that bites worse than soldiers?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_route_dark_t: Is it safe to travel after dark?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_route_carava: Which way do the caravans go?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_route_fewest: Which road gets me through with the fewest questions?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_route_haulin: I'm hauling goods. Which road won't get them taken?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_route_quiet_: Which paths stay quiet these days?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_night_avoid: What should I avoid out here at night?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_night_comes_: What comes out after dark in these parts?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_night_whose_: Whose fires are those out in the dark?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_night_keep_w: Is it madness to keep walking tonight?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_night_sound: What was that sound just now?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_night_watchw: What should I call out so your sentries don't jump me in the dark?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_night_safe_f: Where's the nearest safe fire tonight?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_night_moon_r: Do raids come with the full moon out here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_night_bad_ro: Which roads go bad after sundown?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_blood_still_: I know we've traded blows. I still need directions.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_blood_market: Business is business. Where's the nearest market road?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_blood_blind: You'd rather I wander your lands blind? Tell me what's ahead.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_blood_truce_: Truce for a minute. What's down this road?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_blood_forget: Forget what happened between us. Who patrols this stretch?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_blood_coin: My coin spends the same as anyone's. What's out east?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_blood_missin: Your patrols keep missing me. Where will the next one be?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_field_far_ou: What brings your patrol this far out?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_field_seen_a: Seen anyone else on this road today?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_field_tracks: I crossed fresh tracks back there. Yours?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_field_lost_w: Are you lot lost, or am I?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_field_ground: How far does your ground run out here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_field_trail_: Anything I should know about the trail ahead?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_field_water_: Is there water enough out here for two more days' walking?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_field_walk_a: Mind if I walk with your patrol a stretch?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_field_home_f: You're a long way from home.
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_supply_come_: Where do your supplies come in from?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_supply_short: What are you short of these days?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_supply_next_: When does the next supply run arrive?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_supply_surpl: Can I buy off your surplus?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_supply_bring: If I brought goods to sell, which road should I use?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_supply_store: How deep are your stores running?
dialogue.warfront.opt.intel_supply_guard: Which routes need guarding? I might take the work.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_ask_own_bas: Our walls are for us. You get the wire.
You want the line's address? Earn it or dig for it.
There's a camp. It has a direction. That's all you get today.
The line sits where the digging is. You'll know it by the mud.
Follow the trench-smoke north till your boots sink. Knock loud, walk slow.
Home is where the shovels are. Head that way — tell them the line sent you.
You've earned the walk. Warm food, cold bunks, honest mud. Go on.
Base locations are restricted. Move along.
That information is above your clearance. It will stay there.
Installations are need-to-know. You don't need to know.
Follow the marked road and you'll be met before you're lost.
Cleared for release. Bearing's on your map — announce yourself at the outer marker.
Forward operating site is a short march out. Gate staff will have your name.
Take the maintained road. If a sentry stops you, say you're logged as friendly.
Our tents move. Your questions do not catch them.
Ask the dunes. They keep our address better than I do.
Where do the swallows sleep? Somewhere out of the wind. So do we.
The camp finds its guests. Guests do not find the camp.
Walk toward the evening star until you smell cardamom. The fires will rise to meet you.
The path is under the third ridge, where the shadow pools at dusk. You are expected.
Follow the camel tracks that vanish. Where they end, we begin.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_stonewall_b: Ha. Write your question down, roll it tight, eat it.
You ask where we sleep? Closer than you'd like, friend.
The only map you get is the road out. It's behind you.
Curious one, aren't you. Curiosity fills trenches.
That's line business. Yours is walking.
Even for you, some doors stay shut. Nothing personal — everything's personal, actually.
Ask me about the weather instead. The weather won't get us shelled.
Denied. And the request itself is now in your file.
That question is a threat indicator. Ask another.
You are fishing in a restricted pond, civilian.
Negative. Operational security is not a courtesy I can waive.
Request denied. Standard procedure, nothing personal.
Even friendlies don't get that one. Doctrine before friendship.
Can't release it. What I can do is walk you somewhere safer to stand.
You ask the mirage for its house. Enjoy the search.
A knife asks the sheath where it lives. The sheath smiles.
Dig anywhere. You will find sand, and sand, and then us — too late.
The desert has many rooms and lends none of them.
Some questions are doors. That one is a wall.
Friend, do not carry that answer. It is heavy, and men die of the weight.
Even the tea does not know where the kettle sleeps.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_vague_direc: There's mud in every direction. Pick one.
Somewhere out there. Walk until someone shouts.
There's a road east. It goes east. That's its whole trick.
Settlements come and go out here. Mostly go.
Follow the ruts. Carts are smarter than people about where to walk.
Keep the sunrise on your left shoulder and you'll hit the trade track by noon.
There's a hamlet past the burned mill. They'll sell you bread if you don't mention us.
Consult a map. Not mine.
Navigation assistance is not on offer today.
General bearings only: settlement traffic runs the east road. Beyond that, ask there.
You're inside our operating area. Edges are a day's walk in most directions.
The river road is maintained. The rest I wouldn't certify.
Marked route east, two klicks, then follow the cairns. You'll raise a village by dusk.
Stay on the graded road and you'll pass two of our markers before any trouble.
Every direction is far, walker. Start early.
The land belongs to whoever the land is currently eating.
Roads here are like promises. Some are kept.
There is a well two ridges over. Where there is water, there are people. Sometimes kind ones.
Walk with the wind at your back and you will arrive somewhere. The desert decides where.
Past the white rocks there is a market that asks no names. Mention the shade and pay less.
Follow the old riverbed. Dead rivers still know the way to towns.
Give you our enemy's door? You haven't even earned ours.
No. You'd sell it to them by supper.
That arithmetic isn't for strangers.
The enemy is that way. The details cost more than you've paid.
Lean in. Their camp squats past the ridge — hit it at dawn and count for us.
We've bled for this map. You've bled with us, so look: there. Bring back their banner.
Their walls are where our shells land. Follow the thunder, friend.
Hostile positions are classified. Especially from you.
You don't have the clearance, and frankly you don't have the trust.
Target data is restricted. Assistance in earning access is available.
Negative. That release requires a history of trust you haven't built yet.
Releasing hostile grid to a verified friendly. Copy it once, burn nothing, tell no one.
Enemy encampment plotted at the marked bearing. If you act on it, we never spoke.
You've earned target access. Coordinates follow. Advise you strike with the sun behind you.
You hunt with wolves you have not fed. No.
Our enemies' names are not coins for your purse.
The scorpion does not point out the other scorpion. Professional courtesy.
Patience. Trust ripens slower than dates.
Their fires burn beyond the salt flat. Go in the cold hours; their sentries dream of home.
The vipers nest where the two hills kiss. Strike while the shadow is longest, friend.
We have watched them a season. Now you may borrow our eyes. There — where the crows circle.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_rival_offic: An officer's map is paid for in casualties. Yours isn't the currency.
I brief my line, not strangers with opinions.
Briefings are for people who dig when told. You don't dig.
I've buried men for guessing at this. I won't hand it to you free.
Fine. Officer to irregular: their strength sits past the ford. Numbers favor us. They always do, eventually.
Here's the picture I give my sergeants: enemy there, us here, mud everywhere. Memorize it.
You've carried weight for the line, so carry this: their forward camp, one valley over.
You're asking a commissioned officer to commit a breach. Bold. Denied.
My scouts earn their briefings. You've earned an escort out.
That briefing has a distribution list. You're not on it.
I don't freelance intelligence, civilian. Chain of command exists for a reason.
Command assessment, verbal only: hostile axis runs the low ground. Their camp anchors it. Marked.
I'll authorize a one-time release. Enemy laager at the plotted point. Use it before it goes stale.
Consider yourself a deputized asset. The opposing force masses beyond the tree line — there.
The falcon does not report to the field mouse.
I lead by knowing what others do not. I will keep leading.
A captain's knowledge is his tent pole. Pull it and everything falls.
Ask me for water, for bread, for shade. Not for this.
Come, look at the sand table. This wadi — their camp. This hour — their weakness. Go quietly.
I will tell you what my riders know: the enemy sleeps fat behind the gap in the hills.
You have kept faith with the shade, so the shade opens its hand: their position, there.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_rival_refus: Our wars are our own. Yours is finding the road out.
You ask about our enemies like you aren't one. Funny.
The front doesn't send news. It sends stretchers.
There's a war. It's around. Specifics are for people in it.
Who's winning? The flies. The flies are always winning.
You want battle news, enlist. We issue shovels same day.
Careful, friend. Names of enemies are heavier than they look.
Not yet. Ask me again when your boots have more of our mud on them.
Hostile force data is classified, and you're closer to hostile than force.
Your interest in our enemies is noted. And filed.
No comment, and the asking cost you nothing only this once.
Ongoing operations are not discussed with unaffiliated persons.
There is a conflict. Its particulars are managed. That's your briefing.
I can neither confirm nor locate anything for you today.
Soon, maybe. Trust accrues like interest, and yours is still maturing.
That's one clearance level above us both, friend. Stay the course and it comes.
You ask who we fight. Today, perhaps whoever asks too much.
Our quarrels are old and private, like family debts.
The desert eats armies. Which one is not your concern.
Wars here are like wind. Always somewhere, never where you point.
Who is winning? The sand. The sand is undefeated.
When the tea has been shared more times, perhaps the names will pour too.
Patience, friend of the shade. Fruit picked green sours the whole basket.
Walk with us a while longer. Then we will speak of vipers and where they nest.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_patrol_sche: The patrol comes when it comes. Usually right behind you.
Our rounds are our business. Being found by them is yours.
Rounds pass often enough. Often enough for what? Exactly.
Shifts change when the relief stops complaining and starts walking.
The line walks its wire at all hours. Sleep is a rumor.
Next sweep loops the east track before dusk. Wave early, wave big.
Relief column moves at first light. Travel behind it and you'll have quiet roads.
We double the wire watch after bad nights. Last night was bad. Walk loud today.
Patrol timings are classified. Persisting will classify you.
That's operational tempo. Not yours to know.
Rotations occur on schedule. The schedule is the part you don't get.
Coverage is continuous. Treat every road as watched and you'll be accurate enough.
Patrols are frequent by design. Design is classified.
Between you and the gatepost: south leg turns over at dusk. Cross before, not after.
Next foot patrol sweeps the ridge road within the hour. Friendly faces, if yours stays friendly.
Our long-range element is out two days. Roads west are thinner than usual. Plan accordingly.
We pass when the shadow passes. Try to time a shadow.
Ask the moon when we walk. She keeps our diary.
The watch changes as the wind changes. You will feel it, not see it.
We are behind you more often than ahead of you. Let that schedule your day.
Patrols? We prefer to say the desert strolls, and sometimes we stroll with it.
The riders swing wide of the salt pan until the heat breaks. Travel it at midday, friend.
Our walkers rest at the old cistern near sundown. Pass there and you pass among friends.
Tonight the watch is thick to the north. Keep south of the ridge and the road is yours.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_patrol_refu: Asking about our watch is how people end up counted by it.
Blind spots? We're standing in one. Just you and me. Think about that.
Short-handed, sure. Never too short to handle you.
That question has barbed wire around it.
Watch business stays inside the watch.
Even friends don't get the roster. The roster is how we stay alive.
Ha — you sound like an inspector. Inspectors get shown the nice trench only.
That is exactly the question an infiltrator asks. Noted, timestamped, remembered.
Sentry counts are classified. Your interest in them is now also on file.
Keep probing our watch and the watch will probe back.
Security posture isn't shared. Standing order, no exceptions.
Negative on all of that. The perimeter answers to no questionnaire.
Friend or not, the watch bill stays sealed. It protects you too, believe it.
If our coverage worried me, I'd fix it, not discuss it. It doesn't worry me.
You count our sentries? Count the stars instead. Same use, longer life.
The night has holes only for those we allow to fall through them.
Ask again about our watch and you will meet it personally.
The tent does not show its stitching to the wind.
We watch what needs watching. Currently, that includes you.
Even to a friend, the pattern of the watch is a bride's face. Veiled.
Why count our eyes, friend? Enough are open. Always enough.
This road belongs to whoever holds it. Today: us. Keep moving.
Watched enough to catch you. That's the number that matters.
It's the line's road. We sweep it when the mud allows.
Bandits tried this stretch once. The ditch remembers them.
Carts pass on quota days. Otherwise it's boots and crows.
Our section walks it twice a day, more when the guns get chatty. You're covered till the fork.
Road's ours and it's quiet. The tolls died with the last toll-takers.
Stay on it till the burned oak, then you're past our wire and into luck.
This is a controlled route. You're the current control problem.
Who watches it? You're talking to him. Move along.
Route is under regular observation. Conduct yourself accordingly.
Checkpoint ahead at the bridge. Have your business ready to state.
Bandit activity is suppressed on this corridor. We keep it that way.
Corridor's green through the crossroads. Past that, our coverage thins — stay alert.
You'll hit one checkpoint at the mill. Give them your name; it's in the friendly log.
We run this road on a tight loop. Trouble finds you, hold position — response is fast.
The road is watched. Mostly, right now, you are the thing watched.
Whose road? The road of whoever wakes up still holding it.
Many eyes rest on this road. Not all of them blink.
Tolls, no. Debts, sometimes. The road keeps its own ledger.
Night traffic exists. It prefers not to be discussed.
The road is under our shade to the twin palms. Beyond that, walk like a stranger again.
Trouble avoids this stretch, friend. Trouble knows who it belongs to.
Carts pass on market days under our eye. Join one; company shortens miles.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_terrain.vos: Over the ridge? More war. Under it too, if you dig.
Terrain questions from you make my trigger finger philosophical.
Ridge hides a dead village. Everything useful was carried off, including the roofs.
The valley floods, the forest hides deserters, the caves eat lanterns. Charming country.
Good water at the shattered well, if you boil it and your standards are low.
Past the ridge is a meadow the shells missed. Prettiest thing for miles. Enjoy it for us.
The caves north are dry and deep. We stashed matches there once. Might still be some.
That smoke is ours — cook fires, not signal fires. Somebody finally shot a boar.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_terrain.aeg: Terrain data supports operations. You're not an operation. Yet.
Ask the ridge yourself. Take your time up there in the open.
High ground east is surveyed. Low ground floods seasonal. Plan around both.
The ruins predate all three banners. Structurally unsound, occasionally occupied.
The pass is open but unimproved. Rockfall risk after rain.
Over the ridge: open farmland, one abandoned watchtower, decent sightlines. Safe in daylight.
Reliable water at the spring by the split boulder. We test it monthly. It passes.
Coast is three days on the river road. Two if you don't stop to admire our engineering.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_terrain.sar: Beyond the ridge is more of what is behind you. Disappointment.
The land answers politely to polite guests. You are neither, yet.
The valley holds an old orchard gone wild. The fruit is bitter and the shade is sweet.
Those ruins were a proud town once. Pride is poor mortar.
The swamp can be skirted on the deer paths. Deer are honest guides.
Beyond the ridge a spring hides under the fig roots. Drink deep and thank the tree, friend.
The caves keep cool even at noon. We have slept there; the sand inside tells no tales.
That smoke is a wedding, not a war. This week, at least, the hills celebrate.
Safest way is away. All roads qualify.
Routes are safe until they aren't. You'll find the boundary fast.
East road is dull, which is the best thing a road can be.
Avoid the ford after rain and the tavern after payday.
Caravans hug the ridgeline. Slower, but caravans still exist, so.
Take the sunken lane, friend. Ugly walking, but nobody ambushes a ditch they can't see into.
Go west by the quarry track. Our guns overlook it the whole way. Best escort money can't buy.
Cross the river at the cattle ford, not the bridge. Bridges collect the wrong crowd.
Route planning services are for cleared personnel. Walk where you like. Carefully.
The safest route for you is out of my sector. Any bearing.
Main east road is patrolled and posted. Secondary tracks are travel-at-own-risk.
After dark, movement is discouraged. That's guidance, not a threat.
The river crossing at the mill is inspected and stable. Use that one.
Recommended routing: east road to the crossroads, then the marked trail. Both under watch.
Hauling cargo? Take the convoy road on supply days. Nobody touches what moves with us.
West passage is clean this week. Our patrols just swept it end to end.
Every road is safe until the sand shifts. The sand is shifting.
Ask me tomorrow. Tonight, no road would forgive you.
Travel with the cool hours and the busy birds. Both avoid trouble professionally.
The shortcut exists. It is shorter in distance and longer in regret.
Cross the river where the women wash clothes. Danger avoids witnesses.
Walk the shepherd trail at dawn, friend. It is watched by kind eyes the whole way.
The quiet paths run behind the dunes. Quiet because we keep them so. They are yours today.
Go with the salt caravan when it passes. Its guides owe us shade and will owe you courtesy.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_night_hazar: At night, avoid us. There. Free advice.
The dark hides wolves, deserters, and worse: sentries who startle.
Avoid lights that move and silences that don't.
Night belongs to whoever's most tired of living. Don't compete.
That sound? Wire on wind. Probably. The line finds out at dawn.
Stay near our wire tonight, friend. Shout 'shovels' at the sentry and he'll wave you close.
Our fire's the low red one by the berm. Cold night's shorter with company.
Dawn's maybe four hours off. Sit with the reserve squad; they brew something almost like tea.
After dark, unidentified movement gets one challenge. Sometimes.
Night protocol is strict. You're one silhouette away from learning it.
Avoid the perimeter approaches at night. Sentries challenge once, per doctrine.
Unlit roads are uncontrolled roads. Govern yourself accordingly.
That sound was an animal or a problem. We're paid to assume the problem.
Call out 'traveler, friendly' at any post and hold still. You're in the log; you'll be fine.
Safest fire tonight is our forward picket. Announce early — night watch likes warnings.
First light in five hours. Shelter at the signal tower; the crew expects stragglers.
The night here has our manners. Do not test its patience.
What comes out after dark? We do. You have your answer and your warning.
Avoid still water and still men. Both drown travelers.
The fires you see are stories. Some welcome guests. Some collect them.
Walk loud if you must walk. The night mistakes quiet men for prey — or rivals.
Sleep near the tamarisk, friend. Our night walkers pass it twice and will pass over you kindly.
The moon is with you tonight. Keep her on your right and you keep our blessing.
Come to the low fire with the copper kettle. Night tea is bitter and the company gentle.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_blood_ask.v: Directions? To your grave, gladly. It's nearby and we dug it personally.
Eleven names, and you want a map. The nerve is almost admirable. Almost.
You spilled our blood and want directions. The road out. Fast.
The only thing I'll point at you is already pointed.
You've cost us, and you know it. Ask small questions and walk smaller.
Truce, he says. The dead don't sign truces. But fine — the road's clear to the fork. Go.
You settled some of what you owed, so: east track's safe. We're square until you make us not.
The line remembers your sins and your service both. Today the service wins. Barely. Head south.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_blood_ask.a: You have confirmed kills on this command and questions in your mouth. Astonishing. Leave.
Weapons-free is one order away. Your directions are: anywhere else.
You're red-flagged with casualties attached. No information will be released.
Your record includes our dead. This conversation is over-generous already.
Given your history, cooperation is limited: road's open east. That's all you get.
You've cost this command personnel. I'll answer nothing that helps you cost us more.
Your ledger with us is complicated. Balance says: market road's two klicks south. Don't reset it.
Restitution is noted, casualties are not forgotten. Travel east. Stay visible while you do.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_blood_ask.s: You come to the well you filled with blood, asking to drink. Poetic. Fatal, but poetic.
The sand under your feet holds our brothers. It is listening for your last step.
Directions, from us, for you? The vulture gives better ones. Follow him.
Your hands are red and your tongue is bold. One of these will shorten your road.
We remember what you took. Still — the road east is open. Even debts respect the road.
Bold, to ask. The market track runs past the dry well. Walk it owing us, and walk quickly.
Blood dries, friend, when enough kindness rains on it. East, past the cairns. Go in peace, this once.
The scales between us tremble. I will steady them: safe road south. Do not touch the scales again.
Far from our walls, close to our patience's end. State your business.
Out here there's no wire between us. Remember that.
We walk where the line needs eyes. Today it needs them here.
Seen nobody but crows and you. The crows were better company.
Tracks are ours. If they weren't, we'd be running, not talking.
Long way from home, sure. Home is where the shovel lands. Tonight, that hollow there.
Trail ahead is clear to the second ridge. After that, keep your head on a swivel, friend.
Walk with us to the stream if you like. The pace is miserable and the jokes are worse.
This patrol is tasked. You're an unplanned contact. Don't become an unplanned incident.
Distance from base means nothing. Reach is doctrine.
Routine reconnaissance. That's the whole answer you're cleared for.
Negative contacts today besides yourself. Keep it a quiet log.
Trail ahead is unassessed past the creek. Treat it as such.
We're sweeping the far arc — long walk, good boots. Road behind us is clean, use it.
You can move with the patrol to the waypoint. Stay in file, don't wander off the track.
Fresh water's cached at the leaning pine. Take a fair share and leave the cache covered.
Far from walls, yes. We never had walls. You are far from yours.
The patrol you see is the smallest part of the patrol you don't.
We go where the sand goes. It has been going here lately.
The only tracks that matter are the ones you did not notice.
The trail ahead is honest until the black rocks. After that, it starts telling stories.
Walk with us to the well, friend. The desert is smaller with company and larger with none.
We camp where the wind forgets to look. Tonight, that gully. There is room by the fire.
Ahead the trail is swept and safe. We swept it. Consider it our gift to your boots.
dialogue.warfront.resp.intel_supply_line: Stores are counted, crates are counted, you are counted. Move along.
Supply questions from strangers end up in the wrong ledgers.
Supplies come from sacrifice and a road I won't name. Mostly sacrifice.
We're short of everything except mud and resolve. Standing order.
Grain fetches whatever hungry men pay. So: everything.
Between us — the column comes up the north road on quota days. Sell to me before it arrives, prices are kinder.
Short on salt, nails, and reasons to smile. Bring any of the three and we'll talk numbers.
There's escort work on the ration road if your arm's strong and your questions are few.
Logistics data is more classified than the war itself. File your curiosity elsewhere.
Asking a quartermaster about supply lines is asking to be inventoried. Don't.
Procurement is centralized, distribution is scheduled, and neither is your business.
Shortages exist. Their specifics are managed above your involvement.
Market rates are posted at the trade point. Consult the board, not me.
Resupply convoy runs the graded road twice weekly. Vendors get right of way if they're on the ledger — you are.
Current shortfalls: binding wire, lamp oil, dried fruit. Deliver any and invoice me directly.
Route security contracts are open. Standard rates, paid on delivery confirmation. Interested?
Where does our water come from? The sky. Complain to it.
You count our sacks and I will count your steps. Neither ends well.
Supplies arrive the way dew arrives. Quietly, and gone by the time you ask.
What are we short of? Rain. Always rain. The rest we manage.
Prices here follow the wind. Today the wind is moderate.
The caravans slip in by the old salt path, friend. Meet them at the cistern and trade under our shade.
Bring dates, rope, or good cloth and the camp will open its purse to you gladly.
We pay well for quiet guards on the water road. Quieter the guard, heavier the purse.

dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_doctrine_why: Our way of war? You will meet it soon enough if you keep asking.
Doctrine is for us to know and you to trip over.
We fight the way we bury: often, and without speeches.
Numbers, patience, shovels. Wars are won by whoever runs out of men last. We don't run out.
We trade blood for ground. The rate is bad. The ground stays.
First wave finds them. Second wave tires them. Third wave is arithmetic.
Simple, friend. The line advances until the enemy is tired of killing it. Then we accept his surrender.
They call it cruel. We call it Tuesday. The line holds because there is always more line.
Steel breaks, men break. The quota does not break. That is our whole book of war.
Doctrine is classified. Your curiosity is logged.
You want our playbook? Request denied. Move along.
I don't brief hostiles. That is the doctrine.
Combined arms. Every element covered by another element. No one fights alone.
We commit nothing without support. Shield up, then strike. In that order.
Precision beats mass when precision holds formation. We hold formation.
Short version: never trade lives for ground when you can trade planning for both.
Every action rehearsed, every flank assigned. Improvisation is for people who skipped the briefing.
The doctrine is boring on purpose, friend. Boring wins.
You ask a mirage to explain water. Walk on.
Our way is written in sand. By the time you read it, the wind has answered for me.
The snake does not lecture the mouse.
We do not fight the armies. We fight their patience. Patience always surrenders first.
Strike where they are not, be gone before they are. The desert does the rest.
Heavy armies dig graves for themselves. We only wait by the graveside.
Come, the truth: we are few, so the land fights for us. Sun, thirst, doubt — all our soldiers.
A blade in the dark spends less blood than a wall of shields at noon. We prefer thrift.
We win the hour before the battle, friend. The battle itself is just the receipt.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_doctrine_off: An officer explains doctrine to soldiers. You are not one of mine.
My cadets earn the lecture with blisters. You have earned nothing.
Doctrine, in full: mass decides. Everything else — morale, weather, genius — is decoration.
I spend men the way a smith spends coal. Ugly? Yes. The forge does not care.
Listen, then. War is a scale. We pile our dead on one side until it tips. No one likes the answer. It stays the answer.
I tell recruits this: you are not a hero, you are weight. Be weight where the line needs weight.
Command briefings are not entertainment for flagged civilians.
You are asking an officer to leak doctrine. That question goes in my report.
We synchronize. Infantry fixes, shields break, signals bind it together. Tempo is the weapon.
Commit criteria: superiority confirmed, withdrawal route secured, objective priced. No price, no fight.
Between us: doctrine is a promise. Every soldier knows exactly who covers them. That promise wins wars.
The grand design? Hold the hinge points, let the other two bleed each other, arrive fresh at the end.
The desert has officers too. You are speaking to one. That is all you learn today.
You ask for the map of the wind. Even my own do not carry that.
I command by absence. My fighters know where not to be, and when. The rest arranges itself.
We commit when the enemy is certain of himself. Certainty is the softest armor.
Since you sit with us: my art is choosing which battles never happen. The unfought war is the won war.
I read their supply trails like poetry, friend. Every wagon tells me where they will be weak in ten days.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_founding.vos: Our story is ours. You get the ending if you keep pushing.
History lesson? For you? The past is the one thing we don't spend on strangers.
We were born in a retreat. That is all a stranger needs.
We started as the ones nobody fed. We learned to hold ground because there was nowhere behind us.
Old soldiers of a dead country. The country fell. The line did not.
First there was a winter. Then there were those who dug. The diggers became Vostok.
Sit, friend. We began as leftovers — broken units, one shared pot. The pot is still shared. That's the whole secret.
Grandfathers of the line held a bridge nobody remembers for a country that no longer exists. We keep holding it.
Born from a rout, raised on rations, married to the mud. A poor family, but a big one.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_founding.aeg: Founding records are archived. Access denied.
Our origin is not your business. End of briefing.
You collect histories the way scouts collect maps. I see it. No.
Formed from officers who watched two armies waste themselves and wrote down every mistake.
We began as a study group, believe it or not. The study was: why do armies die? Then we stopped dying.
Founded on a signature, not a battlefield. Charter first, swords after.
The honest version? Survivors of a massacre who swore the next massacre would be scheduled by us.
Our founders were quartermasters and signalers — the people armies ignore. Turns out they were the army.
It began with a ledger of the dead and a vow: never again without a plan. We kept the ledger. And the vow.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_founding.sar: Ask the dunes who made them. They will answer you as I do.
Our beginning is buried where you will never dig.
Strangers wrote three histories of us already. All wrong. Yours would be the fourth.
We were the people the empires marched past. They took the wells and left the sand. The sand proved loyal.
No founding day, no charter. One night the desert had teeth. It has had them since.
We began when the first caravan guard refused to kneel and vanished into the heat. The heat kept him.
Then hear it properly: we are children of the driven-out. The soft lands were taken, so we married the hard one.
Our founding is a story told backward — first the wrong, then the wandering, then the vow. The vow is still warm.
Three wells, nine families, one oath under a cold moon. Everything since is commentary.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_leaders.vost: Names of commanders? So they can be hunted? Clever. No.
Who leads us is above your ears, stranger.
The Marshal commands. We do not see the Marshal. We see the quota. Same thing.
Sergeants run the war. Everyone above sergeant runs the paperwork.
Our Marshal counts every loss personally, friend. They say the ledger is longer than scripture. He reads it nightly.
Officers here eat last and dig with us. The ones who didn't are gone. The mud sorts leadership honestly.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_leaders.aegi: Chain of command is restricted information. Obviously.
You are asking who to target. Denied, and noted.
High command rotates by council. No single head to cut off. That is deliberate.
Orders come down signed and countersigned. Authority is a procedure here, not a person.
The Directorate is five chairs. Any three can act. No throne, no succession crisis, no cult. It's elegant.
My commander once delayed an offensive to recover two bodies. The ranks have not forgotten. That is leadership.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_leaders.sara: You seek a head for the spear. The desert has no head.
Our leaders are like water underground. Felt everywhere, found nowhere.
Elders counsel, captains decide, the desert overrules everyone.
Each band follows its own voice. The voices meet at the wells and agree more often than you'd think.
The one we heed most calls himself the Last Host — every guest under his shade is owed protection. Even, sometimes, you.
Leadership here is a debt, friend. Whoever owes the people most, leads. Our best captain is the most indebted man alive.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_death.vostok: You ask about our dead with our dead on your slate? Bold.
Death is our trade secret. Keep asking and we'll demonstrate.
Count your own dead. Ours are counted.
A soldier dies. The line closes the gap. That is the whole funeral.
We believe dying is like weather. Complaining doesn't change the forecast.
Every name goes in the roll. The roll is read once a year, all night. Nobody sleeps that night.
We think the dead stay in the line, friend. One pace back. On the worst nights you can hear them keeping step.
When it's my turn: write my name, share my vodka, fill my place by morning. Perfect system. I approve of it.
Death owes us nothing and we owe it everything. That's the joke. Someday I'll laugh.
Casualty doctrine is not shared with people who cause casualties.
Our dead are logged. So are their causes. Think about that.
You want to know how we grieve? Watch what happens to those who give us reason.
Every loss gets a file: cause, lesson, correction. Grief is data here. It has to be.
We hold a review after every death. Not to blame. To make it the last of its kind.
Fallen are listed as 'detached duty'. Sentimental, for us. Don't tell anyone.
There's a wall at the great camp with every name since founding. New officers memorize a row before first command.
We believe a death you learn nothing from is the only true defeat. So we learn. Every single time.
When I go, I'll be a line in the ledger and a correction in the manual. That's immortality, friend. The useful kind.
The dead do not gossip. Learn from them.
You have sent people to the sand and now ask what the sand does with them. It remembers. So do we.
Ask your own shadow about death. It stands closer to you than I do.
We say the desert lends us our bodies and calls in the loan without anger. Water returns to the well.
No graves you can find. The dunes hold our fallen, and dunes wander. So do our dead.
Mourning lasts until the next moonrise. Then the name joins the wind. The wind keeps everything.
Since you ask kindly: we believe the dead become the cool hour before dawn. They visit daily. It is enough.
My brother fell three summers back. When the wind moves the tent at night, I pour him tea. Some cups empty by morning.
Death is the one guest who needs no invitation, friend. So we keep the tent tidy and the debts paid.
Why we hold it is our concern. That we hold it is yours.
The ground under your boots is spoken for. Remember that.
This dirt has our dead in it. You do not walk away from a bank holding your savings.
Somebody must hold ground or the war is just tourism. We hold ground.
Truth? The land is poor, the water worse, and we love it the way you love an ugly dog. It's ours.
Every meter here cost a name from the roll. Abandoning it would make the roll a list of accidents. Never.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_land.aegis.n: Territorial rationale is strategic information. Refused.
Why we hold it matters less to you than what happens when it's crossed.
This ground commands the roads, the ridge, and the water. Control those, control the tempo.
We hold what is defensible and drop what is not. No romance, just geometry.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_land.aegis.p: Look at a map sometime, friend — every route worth taking bends through here. We didn't choose it. Arithmetic did.
Home is wherever the perimeter is green. But I'll admit the sunrise over this ridge has grown on me.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_land.sarab.n: You ask why the scorpion keeps the rock it sleeps under. Move along.
The desert is not held. It permits. You are not among the permitted.
The others see empty land. We see the only honest country left — it starves liars and flatters no one.
Every well here has a name older than any army. We stay so the names are not forgotten.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_land.sarab.p: This sand raised us when the green lands turned us out, friend. You do not leave the mother who fed you last.
Stay till dusk and watch the dunes turn gold. Then ask again why we would die here. You won't need to.
Inventory questions from you? That's called scouting. Try elsewhere.
What we carry is what you'd meet. Leave it at that.
Iron, and lots of it. A dead man's fancy sword arms no one. A crate of plain spears arms a platoon.
Our kit is cheap because our doctrine is honest. Anything shiny gets buried with its owner anyway.
The quartermaster's motto: heavy, ugly, plentiful. A Vostok blade won't win a duel, friend. It doesn't fight duels.
Good boots first, then a shovel, then a weapon. In that order of importance. I'm serious about the boots.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_gear.aegis.n: Equipment specifications are restricted. Your interest is noted in the log.
Asking about our kit gets you a file, not an answer.
Standard issue, interchangeable parts, inspection twice daily. A weapon you can't maintain is a decoration.
Matched kit means any soldier can resupply any other in the dark. That wins more fights than sharpness.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_gear.aegis.p: Here's the philosophy, friend: gear is a promise to the soldier beside you. We keep promises polished.
Nothing we field is the finest. Everything we field works every time. Reliability is the luxury.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_gear.sarab.n: You count our blades with your questions. The count will be wrong.
We carry enough. How much is enough? You may find out.
Light kit, long patience. What we do not carry, the desert hides for us along the way.
A heavy soldier is a slow soldier, and a slow soldier in the desert is a landmark.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_gear.sarab.p: Our craft is caches, friend. The dunes are one long armory if you buried it yourself. We have been burying for years.
One waterskin, one blade, one length of rope. The rest is knowing. Knowing weighs nothing.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_banners.vost: Our colors mean stop walking toward them. Lesson over.
You'd learn the banner's meaning fastest by charging it. Not recommended.
Grey field, red bar. The grey is everyone. The red is what everyone pays.
The banner is old, patched, and refuses to fall over. So it's a portrait.
The red bar was a ration stripe first, friend — the mark on the last bread crate of the first winter. We kept it.
New flags are sewn from old uniforms. You might say the dead carry it with us. We do say that, actually.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_banners.aegi: Insignia questions from a flagged individual. Wonderful. No.
The symbol means we're organized and you're observed.
The shield sigil is literal. We are the thing between order and the alternative.
Colors are standardized for recognition at distance. Meaning is secondary to function. Mostly.
Look closely at the shield's border — a chain of small links. Each link is a founding company. None have broken.
The oath is to the charter, not the cloth. Cloth burns. The charter is memorized.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_banners.sara: We fly no banner for strangers to aim at. Think on why.
Our symbol is the empty horizon. Study it on your way out.
Our mark is the crescent of a moon you only see in the deep desert. Those who know it, know.
We sew no flags. We cut our sign into the wind — you have walked past it a dozen times unknowing.
The marks by the wells, friend — three cuts, one hollow. It means a guest drank here and was safe. Oldest law we have.
Our banner is carried in the mind, where rain and conquest cannot reach it. Every child learns to draw it blindfolded.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_victory.vost: Victory looks like your column of the ledger closing. Next question.
We'll describe winning to you after. There's always an after for us.
Winning means the last line standing is ours. We are very practiced at standing.
Victory is when the quota finally reads zero. Nobody alive has seen that number.
Honestly, friend? Victory is a boring harvest, a fat winter, and shovels used for potatoes. We fight for boredom.
The day we win, the roll of names gets read one last time, start to finish. Then we plant over the trenches. That's the plan.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_victory.aegi: End-state criteria are classified. Your speculation is noted.
Victory conditions? Fewer people like you inside the perimeter. We're working toward it.
Victory is defined: secure borders, open roads, verified disarmament of both rivals. Measurable or meaningless.
We don't need a triumph. We need a stable equilibrium with us holding the pivot.
Between us: winning means checkpoints become toll booths and sentries die of boredom. I dream of paperwork.
The war ends when order is cheaper than raiding for everyone involved. We're pricing it that way, deliberately.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_victory.sara: Our victory will not be announced. You will simply notice the silence.
Ask the sand what winning looks like. It has beaten every army yet.
Victory is when the caravans cross unguarded and pay respect at the wells, not tribute.
We do not need their surrender. We need their exhaustion. It ripens on its own.
Winning, friend, is a night market under torches, open to all, safe without one drawn blade. My grandmother saw one. I will.
When the last army leaves the desert to the desert, we will have won. Armies always leave. We only stay.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_recruits.vos: Where we find soldiers is not for someone who unfinds them.
Recruitment? The line feeds itself. Don't ask how.
People come hungry, we feed them, they dig. By spring they're Vostok. It's not complicated.
Volunteers, mostly. Winter is our best recruiter. It has no rival.
I joined for the soup, friend, stayed for the brothers. Most honest army alive — we don't even promise you'll survive.
We take anyone who can lift a shovel and share a pot. The pot part matters more.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_recruits.aeg: Recruitment pipelines are protected information. Standard reasons.
You're not applying. You're mapping. Application denied either way.
Selection, assessment, probation, oath. Half wash out at assessment. That half keeps our standard.
We recruit clerks, farmers, smiths — then build the soldier on top. Character first, skills install later.
You'd stand a chance, friend. We prize people who ask questions before drawing blades. Rarer than courage.
My village burned while two armies argued right of way. Aegis was the one that came back with a plan. So I signed.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_recruits.sar: The desert chooses its own. It has not mentioned you.
We do not recruit. We recognize. You are not recognized.
No one signs anything. You share water, you share risk, and one day you notice you belong.
Families mostly, and the desert's strays. The dunes deliver us the stubborn ones.
I was a caravan boy who watched raiders spare our well for an old mark, friend. I wanted to be the mark. Now I am.
Prove yourself? Carry water to a stranger. Someone is always watching here. That is our welcome and our warning.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_training.vos: Our training is watching. Yours is being watched.
Half-trained, are we? The line will tutor you personally someday.
Training is digging until digging is dreaming. Then formation drill until you turn in your sleep.
First lesson: hold. Second lesson: hold anyway. Third lesson: there is no third lesson.
They trained us to be boring, friend. Panic is interesting. Corpses are interesting. We aim for dull and alive.
You spot a veteran by the boots and the silence before dawn. The fresh ones chatter. Dawn cures it.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_training.aeg: Training standards are internal. Your assessment of our recruits is filed under humor.
Twelve weeks basic, then specialization. A soldier drills their role until improvisation feels like error.
First lesson is signal discipline. A quiet soldier who reports well outlives a brilliant one who doesn't.
One thing training gave me, friend: the checklist. Doubt the mood, trust the checklist. It works on farms too.
We rehearse retreats more than attacks. Anyone can advance. Leaving well is the professional's art.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_training.sar: Our training is invisible. Its results are not. You may meet the results.
We train in the dark, stranger. That answer is complete.
A recruit's first task: cross the flats unseen by three watchers. Some take a season. The desert grades honestly.
We teach stillness first. Anyone can move. The desert only forgives those who know when not to.
My first lesson, friend: bury a date pit, find it a year later. Memory is our armory — the blade part comes quick.
Night drills under no moon, steering by wind on the cheek. You'd be surprised what a face can see.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_roe.vostok.n: Rules? Here's one: enemies who ask about rules are testing them.
Our rules of war are none of your business and all of your future.
Rules exist. Prisoners fed, wells left clean, no fire to homes. Winter makes enough orphans without help.
A truce for the dead is honored. Even them. Even us. Some things are not spent.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_roe.vostok.p: The ledgers call us brutes, friend, but ask around: Vostok never poisoned a well. We plan to drink from all of them.
We keep the old rules. Not from softness — a war without rules never ends, and we intend to finish this one.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_roe.aegis.ne: Asking about our engagement rules sounds like planning around them. Flagged.
The rule that concerns you: approach identified, warned, then handled. You're at 'warned'.
Engagement requires identification, warning where feasible, force proportional. Deviations get investigated. Truly.
White flags are honored and logged. Abuse one and the log follows you forever.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_roe.aegis.po: Our rules exist so young soldiers don't carry home choices no one should carry, friend. The paperwork is mercy.
Yes — even now, a parley flag gets you an escort, not a blade. Test it before you doubt it. Others have.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_roe.sarab.ne: The desert's rules are older than mercy. Do not audition for exceptions.
Rules of war? The sand accepts everyone. That is the only rule we're sure you'll meet.
Guests are sacred, wells are sacred, the dead belong to the desert. Everything else is negotiable at blade's length.
We take captives, treat them as guests, and ransom them fat. Ask around — our hospitality is famous both ways.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_roe.sarab.po: Hear the oldest law, friend: who shares your salt cannot be your prey for a year and a day. We keep it. Strictly.
A truce here is sworn on water, not paper. Paper burns. Thirst is forever. No one breaks a water-oath twice.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_bases.vostok: Our camps' business is our business. Yours is walking away from them.
Counting positions, are we? The wire counts back.
How many, where, how strong — three questions that end conversations here.
Watch posts on the edge, work camps behind, the big camp behind those. Mud arranged in order of importance.
The small posts watch, the middle camps feed the line, the great camp feeds the middle. Everything walks forward.
This position stands because the last one fell. That's the usual founding story.
The great camp, friend? Warm soup, dry bunks, a floor that isn't weather. We tell recruits it's a myth so they don't pine.
Storm shelter? For you we'd find a corner by the stove. The line remembers its friends when the sky turns.
Every wall here was built twice — once wrong, once after the sergeant saw it. All good camps are built that way.
Installation details are restricted. That covers headcounts, layouts, and your next three questions.
Our main camp's location is need-to-know. You need to go.
Perimeter questions from outside the perimeter. Textbook probe. Logged.
Outposts observe, forward bases project, the headquarters coordinates. Tiered, like everything we do.
A forward base is mostly warehouse and signal mast. Unglamorous. Decisive.
Positions follow a standard plan. Any soldier can find the infirmary in any camp blindfolded. On purpose.
The headquarters is quieter than you'd expect, friend. Maps, wire, low voices. Wars are loud; winning is quiet.
Caught in weather, come to the gate and say so plainly. Shelter for civilians is written policy, not charity.
This post has stood four years, rebuilt twice, never abandoned. The rebuild plans predate the first attack. Naturally.
You look for our camps. The desert applauds your ambition.
Our positions? The horizon. All of it. Sleep well.
Even our own do not know every camp. Guess how much you will.
Small fires far apart, and one deep place under the rock where the water lives. That is our whole architecture.
Our forward camps move with the moon. What you found last month is now only warm stones.
The big camp exists. It has a roof of stars and walls of distance. Directions are unavailable.
Since you are a friend: the deep camp is cool, carved, and older than all three armies. We are only its latest guests.
If a storm catches you near our fires, call out 'guest of the well' and stand still. You will be gathered in.
Our camps have no gates, friend. A guest is inside the moment we decide he is. You have been inside for some time.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_sandbags.vos: The sacks stop blades and questions alike. Test neither.
Wouldn't slow you down? The last confident man is under one of them.
Sand is free, stone is not, and a burst sack is mended by breakfast. Poor man's fortress, rich man's results.
There is an art: header, stretcher, tamp, repeat. The sergeant lectures on it for an hour. Don't ask him.
Filled with whatever loses arguments with a spade, friend — sand, clay, once a load of frozen turnips. It held.
A good bag wall drinks a charge like bread drinks soup. Ugly, patient, replaceable. Now you understand our whole army.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_sandbags.aeg: Fortification specifics are restricted. The wall's performance you may take on faith.
Asking what stops a charge, are you. Planning one? Noted.
Sandbags absorb impact and settle under it. A rigid wall cracks once; a soft wall argues indefinitely.
Standard revetment: two bags thick, cross-laid, inspected each watch. Repairs are logged before sunrise.
The manual gives nine pages to bag walls, friend. Page one: 'The wall is the soldier's patience made visible.' Good line.
Come by in daylight and I'll show you the cross-lay pattern. Ten minutes of stacking will save your homestead someday.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_sandbags.sar: Walls interest you. Interesting people study walls. We study interesting people.
Our defenses are not stacked in bags, stranger. They are stacked in years.
We borrow the idea at the wells — sand holding sand. The desert finds it amusing enough to allow.
A bag wall is a dune with discipline. We prefer our dunes wild, but a well must be held.
Truth, friend: we fill ours where we stand, empty them when we leave, and the desert never misses a handful.
The proper emplacement is one the wind rebuilds for you. Stack low, curve into the gale, let the sand volunteer.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_barracks.vos: Our bunks are counted and none are yours. Move along.
Why stay, he asks. Where were you planning to seat us at your table?
Bunkhouse life: snoring in four languages, one stove, cards until the candle dies. You'd hate it. We manage.
The soup is grey, the bread is brave, and complaints go in the suggestion pit. The pit is bottomless.
Cold nights we push the bunks together, stoke the stove, and the sergeant ignores the vodka. Good system, friend.
The cat by the cook tent is Comrade Boots. Outranks me. Eats better too. We're all very proud of him.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_barracks.aeg: Barracks arrangements are internal matters. The tour is cancelled indefinitely.
Our off-duty hours are not your reconnaissance window.
Bunks inspected daily, lights out by bell, mail twice a month if the roads hold. Routine is the comfort.
Rations are balanced, portioned, and beige. Nobody enlists for the food. Reenlistment cooking is a theory of mine.
Between rotations there's a chess ladder, friend. The signals section cheats with hand codes. We let them think we don't know.
Letters from home get read aloud by the stove if you're willing. Mine always are. It keeps the home real.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_barracks.sar: Where we sleep is a question with teeth. Withdraw it.
Our nights are our own, stranger. Yours, out here, may not be.
We sleep in turns, in shade, lightly. A tent is pitched in minutes and mourned by no one.
Meals are dates, flatbread, and whatever the night patrol brings back with a story attached.
Evenings there is tea, someone's grandmother's songs, and stars past counting. Cramped? The sky is our barracks, friend.
The kettle is never empty and never quite yours — it moves down the fire circle. By the third cup you know everyone's sorrows.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_scoff.vostok: Careful. The pit crew is bored today.
Say it again. Slower. My shovel is listening.
Heh. The mouth works. Let's see if the legs are as quick.
Insulting the line. Original. Get in the queue.
Ha! Only friends may talk like that, and you're spending the privilege fast.
Careful, friend. The last wit here got latrine detail. He's still funny. Down there.
Verbal provocation, logged. Escalation would be unwise.
That remark just moved your file to a worse drawer.
Noted for the record. The record is unimpressed.
I'll pretend the wind garbled that transmission. Once.
Bold words inside our response radius, friend. Retract, and we'll laugh it off.
The desert hears everything and forgets nothing. Neither do we.
Words are wind. Some winds strip flesh from bone. Choose yours.
A guest who spits in the well drinks downstream of his manners.
We collect insults like the dunes collect bones. Quietly.
Ah, the friend has thorns today. Sit, drink, and sheathe them before someone less fond of you hears.
Even a rude bird sings, friend. But sing softer near the hawks.
Go. Take the questions with you.
Done? Good. The gate remembers your face.
Off you go. Mind the wire on the left. The left is our joke.
History lesson's over. Homework is staying alive.
Come back for soup night, friend. Bring bread; we'll supply the regrets.
Walk well. The line will hear if you don't.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_exit.aegis.n: Conversation terminated. Depart along the marked path.
Briefing over. Exit is that way, under observation.
Copy. Departing contact, one, no escort required.
Acknowledged. Roads are patrolled through dusk. Plan accordingly.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_exit.aegis.p: Safe roads, friend. Flash a light twice at our towers if trouble follows you.
Copy that. The gate log will read 'friendly departure'. Rare stamp. Keep earning it.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_exit.sarab.n: Leave with the sun on your right and your curiosity behind.
Go. The sand will tell us how far.
May the road be downhill and the questions lighter next time.
Travel between the winds, stranger. It's cooler and wiser.
dialogue.warfront.resp.lore_exit.sarab.p: Go gently, friend. There is tea unfinished here whenever you circle back.
The stars keep the road for you. Walk it while they're generous.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_put_to_: Put me to use. What needs doing?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_outside: Any jobs going for an outsider?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_strong_: I've got time and a strong back. Need anything done?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_task_pr: Give me a task and a price.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_honest_: I hear your side pays for honest work.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_extra_h: Need an extra pair of hands?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_fetch_h: Anything that needs fetching, hauling, or hitting?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_mouth_s: I work fast and I keep my mouth shut. Interested?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_earn_co: Let me earn some coin off you.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_pay_to_: What would you pay me to handle?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_errands: Any errands the soldiers won't do?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_carry_s: I can carry, scout, or fight. Pick one.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_name_on: Is there a contract with my name on it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_dirties: What's the dirtiest job on your list? I'll take it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_beats_f: Got anything that pays better than farming?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_need_co: I need coin. What do you need done?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_ask_somethi: Give me something useful to do out here.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_wor: I want to work off what I did.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_swe: Let me sweat for my mistakes.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_nob: Give me the jobs nobody wants. I've earned them.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_pay: I owe you. Let me pay it in labor.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_squ: There must be work that would square us.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_ugl: Put my debt to use. I'll do the ugly jobs.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_ear: I'd rather earn my way back than beg.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_har: Name a task hard enough to matter, and I'll do it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_han: Let my hands apologize, since my words won't.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_penance_fix: Whatever needs doing to fix this, I'll do it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_grunt_tasks: Hey, got any tasks for me?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_grunt_perso: Can I do a job for you personally?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_grunt_chore: You must have chores you'd pay to skip.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_grunt_shift: Need someone to cover your shift?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_grunt_few_e: Any way I can earn a few emeralds off you?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_grunt_for_h: I'm for hire. Know anyone who's buying?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_grunt_camp_: What work does the camp need done?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_grunt_hand: Could you use a hand with anything?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_grunt_sign_: Where do I sign up for paid work?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_pay_money_f: Let's talk about the money first.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_pay_how_man: How many emeralds are we talking?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_pay_worth_t: Is the pay worth my time?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_pay_what_ge: What do I get out of this?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_pay_up_fron: Payment up front or on delivery?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_pay_bonus: Does the job come with a bonus?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_details_bef: Give me the details before I decide.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_details_fin: Any fine print I should know about?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_details_why: Why hasn't one of your own done it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_risk_killed: Am I likely to get killed doing this?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_risk_kill_m: Will anyone be trying to kill me out there?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_risk_bring: What should I bring to survive this?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_risk_rate: Rate the danger for me, one to ten.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_risk_died: Has anyone died doing this job?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_accept_wher: I accept. Where do I start?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_accept_say_: Say no more. I'll handle it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_accept_talk: Alright, you talked me into it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_accept_befo: I'll get it done before you miss me.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_decline_tro: The pay doesn't cover the trouble.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_decline_tra: No thanks — that job smells like a trap.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_decline_swe: You'll have to sweeten it a lot before I'd touch that.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_coll: Job's done. I'm here to collect.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_dust: Done and dusted. Where's my reward?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_prom: The work is finished, as promised.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_ever: I did what you asked. Every bit of it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_enjo: Finished. And I even enjoyed parts of it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_pock: Your job is complete. My pockets are empty. Fix one of those.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_insp: All done. Inspect it if you like.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_hist: That task you gave me? History.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_deli: Delivered as ordered. Now the coin.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_turnin_hard: It's done, but it cost me. Never again.
Finished the job. Barely walked away from it.
Done. You undersold how ugly that was.
The work's complete. I've got the scars to prove it.
That was worse than you said. It's done anyway.
Job's finished. Next time, warn me properly.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_stil: Still working on that job of yours.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_chec: Checking in. The contract's in progress.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_not_: Haven't forgotten the work. It's coming along.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_unde: The job's underway. Just reporting in.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_half: Your task is half done. Thought you'd want to know.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_take: I'm on it. These things take time.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_stil: Still alive, still on the job.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_not_: Don't worry, the contract hasn't slipped my mind.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_pass: Just passing through. The job's not done yet.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_status_rush: Working on it. What's the rush?
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_abandon_qui: I can't finish this contract. I quit.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_abandon_bey: The work's beyond me. I'm out.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_abandon_tak: Take the job back. It's not happening.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_abandon_wor: I give up on the task. Do your worst.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_abandon_unf: This contract and I are done. Unfinished.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_abandon_kee: I'm walking away from the job. Keep the pay.
dialogue.warfront.opt.orders_abandon_can: Cancel my contract. I've had enough.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_offer.vost: Work? From us? First the ledger, then the labor. That's the order of things.
We give shovels to the trusted and distance to the rest. Guess your prize.
There's always digging, hauling, bleeding. Pick a shift, get a chit.
The front makes work faster than we make hands. Terms are simple, pay is real.
For you? The board's open, friend. Take the job before the sergeant invents a worse one.
The line has work and you have shoulders. A marriage made in mud.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_offer.aegi: Tasking flagged individuals requires oversight. Lucky for you, oversight is bored today.
There is work. There is also your file. They are in tension.
Contracts are posted, scoped, and paid on completion. Interested parties sign here.
We contract civilians for approved taskings. Terms are non-negotiable, payment is prompt.
Good timing, friend. A tasking just cleared for outside hands. Priority one, paperwork zero.
For a proven asset the board opens early. Take your pick of the day sheet.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_offer.sara: Work binds two names together. Yours is not yet a name we tie to ours lightly.
The desert has errands, yes. It prefers messengers it has not been burned by.
There is always a task the wind cannot do alone. Sit, and hear it.
The camp has needs the camp cannot leave to do. Perhaps your feet will serve.
For a friend the good errands surface, like water under the right stone.
The camp trusts your feet and your silence. Both are hired, if you wish.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_offer_pena: Work off the debt? Good. Shovels don't forgive, but they do subtract.
The ledger shrinks for sweat. Slowly. Start today, finish maybe never.
You broke it, you dig for it. That's older than any army.
Debt work is for debtors. Your ledger is clean enough. Take normal wages.
No debt on the books for you. Ask for honest work instead.
Penance? Friend, you owe us nothing but your usual nonsense. Take paid work.
Ha! Your slate is clean. Save the guilt for someone who earned it.
Restitution through labor is provisioned. Completion reduces your infractions. Failure compounds them.
There is a remediation track. It is unpleasant by design. Sign or leave.
Your file has a debit column. Work orders can amend it. Begin immediately.
No open infractions to work off. Normal contracts are available instead.
Remediation applies to flagged files. Yours is not. Ask for normal tasking.
Your record is green, friend. There is nothing to atone for. Take the good contracts.
Penance requires guilt on file. You have commendations instead. Different queue.
You wish to carry water back to the well you salted. Good. The bucket is heavy. Begin.
Debt walked in on your feet. It can walk out the same way, one errand at a time.
The sand accepts labor where it will not accept words. We will watch you sweat.
You owe the camp nothing that work would repay. Take an honest task instead.
Penance without sin is theater. The desert dislikes theater. Ask for plain work.
What debt, friend? The fire speaks well of you. Work for wages, not forgiveness.
Your shadow is welcome here. Save your penance for harder rooms.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_redirect.v: I don't hand out work. I barely hand out words to you.
Ask the officer. Bring a helmet — his mood throws things.
Not mine to give. The officer holds the chits.
Work comes from the top. I just do it. Try the command tent.
If I hired you, the sergeant would hire my hide. Officer's tent, friend.
Ha — I'd pay you my whole wage, all three buttons of it. See the officer.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_redirect.a: Tasking authority sits above my rank and your reputation. Move along.
I don't issue contracts. I especially don't issue them to flagged files.
Contracts come from officers or supply. I'm neither. Follow the chain.
Above my authorization. The duty officer handles civilian tasking.
Wish I could hire you myself, friend. Chain of command says see the lieutenant.
I can vouch, not hire. Take my good word to the duty officer.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_redirect.s: The hand that pays is not this hand. Ask elsewhere, and softly.
I keep watch, not purses. And on you, I keep more watch than most.
Errands flow from the elder tents. I am only a rope in the well.
Ask the one who keeps the seal. My work is watching horizons.
For hiring, seek the keeper of the seal, friend. Tell them the night watch smiled on you.
My purse is thin as morning shade. The elder tent has the fat one.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_pay.vostok: It pays in fewer people scowling at you. Also some coin.
The rate is posted. The grudge discount comes off your end, not ours.
Emeralds on completion, no advances, no widows' fund for outsiders.
It pays enough to complain about. Payment on delivery, always.
Fair coin and first pull at the stew pot, friend. The stew is the real wage.
It pays honest, plus the sergeant forgets one thing you owe him. Negotiable which thing.
Compensation is scale rate minus your risk premium. The premium is you.
Payment is on the sheet. Consider being offered work at all a concession.
Rate is fixed per the tasking sheet. Emeralds on verified completion.
Compensation posted with the contract. No completion, no disbursement.
Full scale plus the allied bonus, friend. Finance grumbled. I insisted.
Top rate for you, and I'll expedite the disbursement paperwork myself.
It pays what the desert pays: enough to reach the next well. For you, barely that.
Coin at the end, and the end only. Trust is not part of the wage.
The purse is fair and opens on completion. The desert honors finished things.
Payment waits at the end of the errand, like shade at the end of a road.
For you the purse opens generously, friend. The elders remember who runs well.
Good coin, and a place by the fire when it's done. The second is worth more.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_details.vo: Details are for the trusted. You get the shape: go there, do it, come back changed or don't.
The job is simple. Watching you attempt it will be the entertainment.
It's on the chit: what, where, when. The why is above both of us.
Simple work, ugly conditions. Everything here is that sentence.
Sit, friend. Here's the map, the names, the shortcut the sergeant pretends is secret.
Full picture, no varnish. You've earned the honest briefing.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_details.ae: You receive the minimum brief. Operational context is need-to-know. You need to go.
Specifics on acceptance. Your clearance covers the destination and the deadline. Nothing else.
Brief is on the sheet: objective, boundary, timeline. Deviations void payment.
Scope is defined and non-negotiable. Read twice, sign once.
I'll walk you through the full annex, friend. Including the part command marked optional-to-share.
Here's the brief plus the field notes from last attempt. Learn from the last man's afternoon.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_details.sa: You will know the road when you are on it. Before that, knowing is a privilege.
The errand explains itself to those who begin it. Begin, or leave.
The task is a story with three parts: the going, the doing, the returning. Hear them in order.
Details are water. We pour when the cup is held steady. Hold steady.
Come close, friend. I will draw the whole road in the sand, wells and dangers both.
For you, the story has no missing verses. Ask anything twice if you need.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_risk.vosto: Dangerous? Everything here kills something. Mostly time. Sometimes visitors.
You might die. We won't. That's the risk summary.
Risk is weather. Dress for it. Bring bandages and low expectations.
Somebody's done it before. Somebody's also not come back. Averages out.
Honest, friend? It bites. Pack iron, walk loud, and you'll outlive it.
The job's survivable. I'd send my brother. I don't like my brother, but still.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_risk.aegis: Threat assessment is classified. Your survival probability is your own project.
Risk exists. Mitigation is available to personnel. You are not personnel.
Threat level moderate, mapped, and printed on the sheet. Read the sheet.
Normal field risk. Casualty history: within tolerances. Yours may vary.
Straight answer, friend: two known threats, one bad crossing. I've marked all three.
