Manageable if you move at dusk and keep the ridge. That's free intel, don't spend it all.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_risk.sarab: The desert is always hungry. Whether it eats you is between you and the desert.
Danger walks that road, yes. It may recognize you as kin and pass by.
Every errand has teeth. This one's are small, but it has many.
The road is safe as roads go. Roads go badly sometimes.
I will not send a friend blind. There is one viper on that path — here is where it sleeps.
Small danger, well-mapped. Walk the cold hours and it will miss you, friend.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_accept.vos: Taken, then. Fail and the ledger grows teeth.
Good. Work hard. We'll count the result, not the effort.
Chit's yours. Come back done or don't come back confused.
Signed and shouldered. The front thanks you in advance, quietly.
Ha, that's the spirit! Go, and bring the good news before the bad weather.
Knew you'd take it, friend. The stew will wait for you.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_accept.aeg: Contract logged. Deadlines are enforced. Excuses are not processed.
Accepted and flagged for monitoring. Perform accordingly.
Contract is active. Report on completion for verification and payment.
Acknowledged. Tasking is yours. The clock is running.
Excellent. Tasking assigned to our best available civilian. That's you, friend.
Logged and cleared, friend. Radio silence means you're winning.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_accept.sar: So the errand has your name now. Names and errands return together, or not at all.
Go. The task watches you now, as we do.
It is agreed. The road knows you're coming. Walk it well.
The errand is yours. Return with it finished and the fire will be warm.
Good, friend. May the wind push your back and the sun forget your face.
The camp sleeps easier with this in your hands. Go gently and swift.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_decline.vo: Refusing work. Noted in the big sad book of you.
Fine. The trench misses no one.
Suit yourself. The job won't cry. Jobs never do.
Declined, then. It'll still be here, uglier, tomorrow.
Ha, smart. That job smelled bad to me too. There'll be better.
No harm, friend. The board refills like a bad well.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_decline.ae: Declination recorded. Availability rating adjusted downward.
Copy. Removing you from consideration. Some lists you want to be on. This was one.
Understood. Contract returns to the pool.
Declined and logged. No penalty, no pay, no problem.
Fair call, friend. Not every tasking deserves you.
No stress. First refusal on the next one is still yours.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_decline.sa: You refuse. The desert shrugs. The desert has a long memory for shrugs.
As you wish. Some doors close softly. Listen how softly.
Then the errand waits for other feet. Peace on yours.
A task refused is a story unwritten. Go find your other story.
Wise to know your roads, friend. Another errand will suit you better.
No shadow falls from an honest no. Sit, drink, choose again another day.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_turn_in.vo: Done? Checked. Adequate. The ledger moves one grudging notch.
It's done, yes. So is the arithmetic. Payment, minus nothing, plus nothing.
Verified. Coin's counted twice, take it once.
Work confirmed. The front notices done things. Briefly, but it notices.
Look at that — finished clean! Coin, stew, and the good bench by the stove, friend.
Done like a Vostok veteran. Take the pay and the compliment. Both are rare.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_turn_in.ae: Completion verified. Payment disbursed. This improves your ledger, not my mood.
Confirmed done. Transaction closed. Punctuality noted despite priors.
Deliverable verified against the sheet. Payment released. Clean work.
Objective confirmed complete. Disbursing now. Aegis honors its contracts.
Textbook execution, friend. Full pay plus the performance rider. Signed happily.
Verified, exemplary, filed. If you ever want a uniform, I know a recruiter.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_turn_in.sa: The errand returned finished. The purse opens exactly as far as promised. Exactly.
Done is done. Coin is coin. The rest of the ledger is a different afternoon.
The task came home whole. The purse honors it. Well walked.
Finished as promised. The desert respects a kept word. So do we.
Beautifully done, friend. Coin, dates, and the story told at the fire tonight — you're in it.
The errand sings your praise. Take the purse and the shade both.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_turn_in_ha: It cost you? Everything costs. Welcome to the economy. Here's the pay.
Scars are receipts. Keep them, spend the emeralds.
Rough jobs make short stories and long drinks. Pay's all there.
You look like the job won on points. But you finished it. That's the whole test.
You went through it, friend. Sit. Stew first, coin second, complaining all night — earned.
Ugly work done well. The line drinks to exactly that. You're the toast tonight.
Field conditions exceeded the brief. Regrettable. Compensation unchanged. Also regrettable.
Hardship acknowledged. Payment is per contract. Sympathy is not a line item.
Brief underestimated the threat. That feedback goes up the chain. Payment goes to you.
Noted for the after-action: conditions severe. Disbursing full rate.
That tasking went sideways and you still delivered. Hazard bonus approved, friend.
You brought it home through the worst of it. Full pay, my respect, and the medic — any order you like.
The road bit you. Roads do. The purse is the same size regardless of teeth.
You bled for it. The desert drank. The contract is still just a contract.
Hard roads make honest messengers. The coin is yours, the ache is also yours.
The errand took its toll at the gate. All errands have gates. Payment in full.
You gave the road blood and it gave you passage. Sit, friend — salve, supper, and the full purse.
The fire heard the road was cruel. It saved you the warm side. Coin's in the pouch, double-knotted.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_status.vos: Still unfinished? The ledger yawns. Finish.
In progress is a place between useful and useless. Move.
Good. Work slow, work sure, work done. Pick two.
Progress noted. The front's still here. So is the deadline.
Take the time it takes, friend. Done right beats done twice.
Steady on. The stew keeps. The job shouldn't, but the stew keeps.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_status.aeg: Status logged. Reminder: contracts age poorly. So do second chances.
In progress, acknowledged. The deadline does not share your patience.
Status received. Continue per the brief. Report at completion.
Copy your progress. No changes to the tasking.
Good copy, friend. Need anything from our end — maps, rations, a kind word?
Progress logged with a green mark. Carry on and stay off the skyline.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_status.sar: The errand is still walking, then. Errands that walk too long start to wander.
We hear you. The task also hears you. It is waiting to be finished.
The road is long, we know. Walk it to the end and the end will pay.
A task in the hand ripens. Do not let it rot.
No hurry, friend. The desert finishes nothing in a day but the dead.
Walk it at your pace. The fire keeps a place and the purse keeps its weight.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_abandon.vo: Quitting. Of course. The ledger writes it in the heavy ink.
Dropped like a cold shovel. We'll remember who dug and who didn't.
Abandoned, then. The job returns to the pile. Your name returns to ordinary.
Fine. Some backs aren't built for some loads. Noted without ceremony.
Eh, it happens, friend. Better a dropped job than a dropped body. Next one's better.
The line forgives a quit faster than a lie. You told it straight. Good enough.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_abandon.ae: Contract voided. Reliability rating amended. The amendment is unflattering.
Abandonment processed. Future taskings will reflect this datapoint.
Contract returned to the pool. No payment, a routine notation, nothing personal.
Voided as you asked. The paperwork forgives faster than the officers.
Voiding it clean, friend. Your record holds. Everyone drops one.
Understood. I'll mark it weather-related. Weather takes many forms.
dialogue.warfront.resp.orders_abandon.sa: You set the burden down in the open desert. Someone must fetch it now. That is remembered.
An errand released midway is a bird with one wing. Ugly thing to leave behind.
The task returns to the camp unfinished. The camp sighs and carries on.
So the road refused you, or you refused it. Either way, it ends here.
Set it down, friend. Some loads argue with the shoulder. No shame at this fire.
The errand goes back to the pile, your name stays warm. Rest, then try a kinder road.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_dig_u: Nice uniform. Did you lose a bet?
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_dig_s: Do they teach you to scowl like that, or is it natural?
You smell like a long campaign.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_dig_h: That helmet's a size too big.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_dig_s: Do you practice standing around, or is it a gift?
Your sergeant must be so proud.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_dig_g: How's the glamorous soldier life treating you?
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_dig_s: Bet you drew the short straw for this post.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_dig_b: You look bored out of your skull.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_doc_v: Your generals spend men like loose change.
Digging holes and dying in them — that's the whole plan, right?
Your quota's just a butcher's bill with extra steps.
The line holds because nobody's smart enough to run.
How many of you die for each mile of mud?
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_doc_a: All your procedures, and you still bleed like everyone else.
Do you file a form before you're allowed to think?
Your precious doctrine is just cowardice with paperwork.
Radio discipline, ration discipline — do they ration your spine too?
Your ledgers won't remember you, you know.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_doc_s: Hiding in the sand isn't strategy, it's cowardice.
All those proverbs, and not one straight answer in your whole camp.
Patience is what you call losing slowly.
Your mirages don't scare anyone who owns a map.
Ambush is just a coward's word for murder.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_m: You're a disgrace to whatever mother raised you.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_f: Your whole company isn't worth one honest farmer.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_s: I've scraped better soldiers off my boots.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_a: Your dead comrades would be ashamed of you.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_l: Everyone laughs at your kind behind your back.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_t: You're nothing but a hired thug with a flag.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_c: Your commander is an idiot and you know it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_g: This land will be glad when your lot is gone.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_s: You fight for scraps and call it honor.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_d: I've seen deserters with more dignity.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_c: Your cause died years ago. You're just too dumb to notice.
Cowards, all of you, dressed up as soldiers.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_f: You take orders from fools and call it duty.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ser_h: History won't even bother to forget you.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ban_f: That banner of yours would make a decent floor rag.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ban_s: I'd spit on your flag if it were worth the spit.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ban_b: Your colors look better burning, I'd bet.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ban_l: That rag on the pole — someone's laundry?
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ban_n: I've blown my nose on finer cloth than your banner.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ban_g: Your flag stands for nothing but graves.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ban_s: One day I'll take that banner home as a souvenir.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_ban_t: Whoever stitched your colors wasted good thread.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_s: Keep talking and I'll shut your mouth for good.
You should sleep lightly from now on.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_k: I know where your patrols walk. Think about that.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_t: One day soon you'll turn around and I'll be there.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_w: Your walls won't protect you from me.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_b: I've buried tougher men than you.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_c: Count your friends tonight. The number's going to shrink.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_n: Cross me again and they'll never find you.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_w: I could end you right here and walk away whistling.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_b: Your kind bleeds easy. I've checked.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_l: Tell your commander he's on my list.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_b: Next time we meet, bring help. You'll need it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_thr_p: I'm the reason soldiers pray before patrol.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_grv_b: I'll burn your base down with everyone in it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_grv_h: I'm going to hunt your squad down one by one.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_grv_b: By winter, your whole company will be bones.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_grv_c: I'll make your commander watch while I take everything.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_grv_d: Every one of you dies. I'm just deciding the order.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_grv_s: I'll salt your fields and poison your wells.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_grv_c: Your people will curse the day they took this land.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_grv_n: When I'm done, no one will remember your names.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_prv_s: Let's settle this right now, you and me.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_prv_t: Come on then. Show me what your training's worth.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_prv_f: I'll give you the first swing. You'll need it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_prv_c: Fight me, or admit you're a coward.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_prv_a: Your move. Or are you all talk?
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_prv_r: Right here, right now. Let's go.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_prv_i: I've been itching for this all day. Come on.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_prv_m: Make me leave. If you can.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_sqd_a: All of you at once. I'll wait.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_sqd_f: Your whole squad against me. Fair fight, finally.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_sqd_c: Every one of you cowards, come and get me!
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_sqd_t: I'll take your whole patrol apart right here.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_sqd_l: Which of you dies first? Line up.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_bld_d: Your friends died easy. You will too.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_bld_b: I remember how the last one begged.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_bld_e: Want to end up like the others I put down?
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_bld_b: How many of yours have I sent home in boxes now?
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_bld_w: Tell the widows I said hello.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_bld_f: The ones I killed? They fought better than you look.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_bld_h: I've made a hobby of your people.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_bld_l: Careful. You know what happened to the last patrol that annoyed me.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_bld_a: Maybe I'll add you to my count today.
dialogue.warfront.opt.provocations_rank_: They give stripes to anyone these days, huh?
An officer? You? Who did you bribe?
Does the fancy plume come with a brain?
You're a grunt because thinking scared you, right?
Do they let the grunts talk, or should I find your handler?
How's the war going from behind your ledger?
dialogue.warfront.resp.provocations_mild: Funny. Write it on your ration card. Oh, wait — you don't get one.
Keep the jokes. You'll want something to say when the mood here turns.
The uniform survived three owners. Show respect for the fabric.
Bored, yes. Boredom out here is the good outcome. Don't fix it.
Ha. The scarecrows work for us too. Better hours than the infantry.
From you, friend, I'll allow one joke a day. That was it. Spend tomorrow's wisely.
The helmet is big so the laughs fit inside. Old army trick.
My sergeant IS proud. Mostly of my digging. It's a narrow pride.
Humor noted. Filed under provocation, minor. The file grows.
Mockery of personnel is a poor use of your remaining goodwill.
The uniform meets specification. Your opinion doesn't alter specification.
Standing here IS the job. Deterrence looks boring right up until it isn't.
If that was wit, transmission received. No further response warranted.
Ha. Log that one under 'friendly banter, tolerated.' Once.
The scowl is standard issue. The smile costs extra and you haven't paid.
Careful, friend — I'm allowed exactly one joke per shift and I'm saving mine.
The jester walks far from home. Jesters have accidents on long roads.
Laugh. The desert collects laughter and returns it with interest.
The camel also mocks its driver, and still it carries the load. Speak on.
A dull knife makes noise on the stone. A sharp one is quiet. Consider which you are.
My boots do not match because the road does not match. Practical, not poor.
Ah, the friend arrives with thorns today. Sit; we will trade them for figs.
You smell a long campaign on me? Good nose. It was a very long campaign.
Teasing is a guest's spice, friend. A pinch flavors. A handful ruins the pot.
dialogue.warfront.resp.provocations_doct: You mock the line with our blood already on you. The count just grew teeth.
Say 'quota' again. I'll show you where your name fits in it.
The line buried better critics than you. It has room for reviews.
We spend men, yes. We're rich in what matters. You're spending something rarer: luck.
Every mile of mud costs. We pay. That's why the mud is ours.
Smart ones run, you say. The runners are dead too, friend. At least ours died facing forward.
The plan is simple because simple survives shelling. Complicated dies with its author.
From a stranger, that's spit. From you, friend, it's a bruise. Pick your words like footing.
You've eaten at our fires and you talk like the enemy's pamphlets. Disappointing.
Careful. The line forgives its friends much. Not everything.
Doctrine mockery from a flagged killer. The recommendation on your file just changed.
Keep talking. You're writing the authorization I've been waiting for.
The paperwork you mock is why our dead are few and yours will be counted precisely.
Cowardice with paperwork still holds every crossroads you need. Sit with that.
Procedure is what's standing between this conversation and a very different one.
We bleed, yes. Rarely, and on schedule, and never for free.
Your critique is noted, unsigned, and unqualified. Dismissed.
That's beneath you, friend. The doctrine you mock has kept you alive in this sector twice.
I'd debate you, but insulting the manual to the man holding it is just poor tactics.
One warning, because I like you: the ledger hears everything. Even jokes.
You call us cowards with our blood drying on your hands. The sand is done waiting.
Mock patience once more. Learn how suddenly patience ends.
The map you own shows where things are. We are never where things are.
Call it hiding. The ones who called it hiding before you are under the dunes now.
The straight answer you want is a straight road. Straight roads are where ambushes live.
Losing slowly, winning slowly — the desert doesn't rush and neither does its verdict.
Murder announces itself. The ambush merely arrives. Words matter less than outcomes.
From a friend, that thorn goes deeper. Pull it back out, and we will call it the wind talking.
You have sat in our shade and now you spit toward it. The shade notices, friend.
Even the fig tree drops one bitter fruit. I will assume that was yours.
dialogue.warfront.resp.provocations_seri: Loud words from a debtor. Your account with the line is overdrawn and collections are near.
Insulting the dead's comrades, with your record. Even the crows are embarrassed for you.
Keep going. Every word makes the eventual arithmetic easier to enjoy.
The line has been called worse by artillery. But artillery could back it up.
Hm. Words are cheap. Ours are cheaper: leave.
You insult a wall. The wall stands. That's the whole exchange.
Brave mouth, unescorted body. Rare combination. Usually brief.
That's how you talk to us now? The mud remembers who it warmed, friend.
The line took you for a friend. Friends get one such sentence free. It's spent.
Verbal hostility from a red-flagged subject. You are assembling your own case file.
Every insult is logged. The log is nearly thick enough to act on. Continue.
Slander of personnel: recorded. Response: pending. Behavior: yours to correct.
You mistake restraint for weakness. Restraint is a setting. It changes.
Opinion registered. Its influence on anything: zero.
This command has survived sieges. It will survive your vocabulary.
Insulting the garrison at the garrison. Bold logistics on your part.
That's a strange way to thank the people who keep your roads open, friend.
I'll assume a bad day and delete the transmission. Once.
Loud insults from a marked man. The desert has heard your voice. It can find it again.
Spend your words, killer. They are the last coins in your purse.
The dog barks at the caravan. The caravan does not vote on it.
Your tongue digs quickly. Tongues make poor shovels and worse graves.
Wind through a tent flap. Loud, brief, forgotten by morning.
We are called cowards by everyone we outlive. It is a long, quiet list.
Honor, scraps — name them as you like. We eat, we endure, we remain.
A friend's insult cuts with a familiar knife. Sheathe it, and we will drink to forgetting.
The kettle has poured for you, and this is the toast you bring? Try again, friend.
dialogue.warfront.resp.provocations_bann: That banner wrapped our dead — the ones you made. Touch it with one more word.
Mock the colors, blood-debtor, and the quota closes around your name today.
Men froze holding that rag so you could sneer at it. They'd trade places with you gladly.
The banner's seen shellfire. Your opinion registers somewhat lower.
Careful. Cloth is cheap. What it's soaked in isn't.
Laundry, ha. It's washed in worse than soap, friend. Walk away from this topic.
Even in jest, not the banner. That's the one wire you don't test with us.
The thread you mock stitched shrouds too. Change the subject while it's still changeable.
Desecration talk from a hostile-flagged subject. You are volunteering for consequences.
The colors you threaten fly over people authorized to answer threats. Recall that.
That standard represents the command structure. Contempt for it is contempt logged at the top.
Souvenir. Noted. Attempts on regimental colors carry the maximum response. All of it.
The flag is inventory, the meaning isn't. Insult neither on this ground.
Colors stay up through worse weather than sarcasm.
Friend, there are jokes we trade and jokes we don't. The colors head the second list.
I'd let that pass, but the flag outranks us both. Retract it.
Our banner shaded the graves you dug for us. Spit, and join what you planted.
The cloth you mock has your name sewn in it now. Thread pulls both ways.
The banner survived three empires of better insults. It will outlast your mouth.
Burn our colors? Fire is our cousin. It knows whose side it sleeps on.
The cloth is old because nothing has managed to take it down. Meditate on that.
You call it a rag. Rags wipe up spills. Ours has wiped up armies.
Not the banner, friend. Even the shade has bones, and you just stepped on one.
The weaver of those colors fed you last month. Swallow the joke with her bread.
dialogue.warfront.resp.provocations_thre: Say it. Give me the excuse. The shovels are already warm.
Threats, from you, with the count where it stands? The line was hoping you'd say that.
You threaten a trench system, alone, in the open. Poets die like this too.
Sleep lightly, he says. We haven't slept since the war started. Your move was pre-owned.
Threats are a loan against your future. The line always collects.
Noted. Filed between the weather and the lice as things that might kill us.
You know where our patrols walk? Good. They'll know where you sleep. Fair trade.
Threatening us, friend? The mud between us must mean less to you than it does to us.
That word choice costs you warmth at our fires. Keep spending and see.
Threat received from flagged subject. Weapons posture updating. Final chance to retract.
You just met the threshold. What happens next is procedure, not anger.
Threat logged verbatim. Response authorization is now one signature away.
You've threatened a garrisoned force with a knife and confidence. The math is public.
That statement meets the definition of a threat. Definitions have consequences here.
Your list, your promises — all transcribed. Aegis archives outlive their subjects.
Advisory: threatening a soldier at his post is the fastest downgrade available.
From a friendly, that's either a bad joke or a worse decision. Clarify. Now.
I'll mark it as stress and strike it. The second one stands forever.
Threaten us again. The sand under you is already listening for the fall.
Good. Announce yourself. The trap prefers informed guests.
You threaten the desert's own. The desert heard. It is very good at waiting.
Loud promises travel far here. So do we, and more quietly.
Men who tell the scorpion their plans make the scorpion's work simple.
Your last quiet days, ours — the desert decides whose. It has never once consulted a threat.
We will not find you, you say? We do not find people. People arrive at us.
A threat from a friend is a crack in a water jar. Mend it now, while the water remains.
The shade withdraws from words like those. Feel the sun on your neck? Choose again.
dialogue.warfront.resp.provocations_grav: Burn our base? You'll be part of the foundation before the first spark.
The order of who dies is set, debtor. You wrote yourself to the top just now.
Whole companies have promised us bones. We compost promises out here.
Salt our fields? We farm mud and casualties. You can't poison what's already bitter.
That's not a threat, it's a confession with a delivery date. The line will be waiting.
Big words. The winter you promise us has tried every year. We're still here to shovel it.
You'd say that to us? Then the friendship was ration paper. It burns fast.
The line just moved you from one list to the other. There's no third list.
Mass-casualty threat, on record, from a known hostile. Restraint is now rescinded.
You've stated intent to destroy this command. Doctrine has one page for that. Short page.
That statement upgrades you to a strategic concern. Strategic concerns get resolved.
Threats against the installation trigger standing orders. They do not expire and do not forgive.
You just described a war crime to a witness in uniform. The report writes itself.
Noted, escalated, and flagged at command level. Your name now briefs generals.
Whatever trust existed is administratively void. Effective immediately.
That sentence ends every courtesy this sector owed you. Confirmed and logged.
Poison our wells? The wells already whisper your name. Water has a long memory.
Speak of our deaths once more and the dune will speak of yours first.
You threaten fire in a land of sand. We have hosted fire before. It left hungry.
Curse the day, curse the land — the desert has swallowed louder curses with its breakfast.
No one remembers our names now, walker. That is the entire trick. You threaten smoke.
Your promise is large. The desert measures men against it while they sleep.
So the guest burns the tent in his heart. The shade hears, friend, and the shade withdraws.
Between us there was tea and salt. You have poured out both. What remains is the desert.
dialogue.warfront.resp.provocations_prov: Finally. The count settles today.
You asked. The line answers.
Fine. One more for the quota.
Short fight. Long ditch.
So be it. Dig your own after.
The mud takes everyone eventually. You've just volunteered early.
Wrong trench to spit into.
So the friend wants the shovel's edge. Grief later. Work now.
You were one of ours in everything but the ledger. The ledger wins.
Weapons-free. At last.
Authorization: granted. By you.
Contact is now kinetic. Copy.
You initiated. The report will read exactly that.
Compliance failed. Engaging.
ROE satisfied. Regrettable. Proceeding.
This was avoidable. Was.
Friendly status revoked. Engaging under protest — but engaging.
You forced the one order I hoped to never file on you.
The debt collects itself now.
The sand opens. In you go.
As the fool insists, the desert obliges.
You called for the storm. It was already behind you.
So the moth demands the flame. Granted.
The blade regrets nothing. Neither shall I.
You chose the short story. It ends here.
You break the salt between us. The pieces are sharp. Feel them.
The shade loved you, friend. The shade will still bury you.
All of us at once — the only prayer of yours we'll answer.
The whole line heard the debtor volunteer. Take him.
The whole section? Lads, we've been challenged by a hero. Bury him with honors.
You counted us and still spoke. Arithmetic was never your friend.
Squad — up. The gentleman insists.
One against the line. The line accepts. The line always accepts.
You'd raise your hand against all of us who fed you? Then all of us answer.
The whole line mourns what you were. Briefly. Boys — shovels down, blades out.
Section: weapons-free on the flagged subject. Execute.
All units, hostile confirmed by his own transmission. Engage.
Squad, form on me. The subject has requested a demonstration. Provide it.
You challenged a fire team, alone. This will be brief and well-documented.
All stations: contact initiated by subject. Weapons out. Engage.
One man, whole squad. Doctrine has a word for this: cleanup.
Team — former friendly has gone hostile by declaration. Standard response. Go.
Every courtesy is now void, and every blade here is on duty. You chose the audience.
Brothers — the marked one calls for us all. The sand agrees. Take him.
He shouts at the whole desert. Show him how much desert there is.
You challenge everyone in the shade at once. The shade empties. Behind you.
Riders — the loud one has invited the entire night. Deliver it.
One voice against many knives. The proverb ends the usual way. Come, all of you.
The whole camp heard the invitation. The whole camp arrives.
He turns on every hand that poured for him. Then every hand answers. Rise.
You were a friend to each of us, and you spit at all of us. All of us reply, then.
dialogue.warfront.resp.provocations_bloo: You joke about our dead to my face. Reach for anything. Please.
Eleven names, and now comedy. The twelfth entry is standing very close to me.
The boxes you brag about — we carried them. Remember that when the dark comes for you.
Keep the widows out of your mouth or lose the mouth.
Boasting about our dead is one wire past clever. Step back over it.
The count between us was cooling. You just blew on the coals. Your funeral. Possibly literally.
They fought better than I look? They taught me. Come find out how well.
You'd mock the graves and drink at our fire? Pick one. Forever.
The line was learning to forget your debt. It just relearned it, word for word.
You are confessing to casualties, in uniform hearing, with a smile. Perfect testimony.
One more sentence about our dead and doctrine handles the punctuation.
Casualty mockery from their killer. The file is now a case. Cases close.
Names, dates, next of kin — we have them all memorized. Your jokes are evidence.
Those personnel had records, families, and comrades on this wall. Choose your next words.
Bragging about kills to the deceased's unit. Tactically illiterate. Morally worse.
Your count is accurate. So is ours. Ours includes projections.
We rebuilt trust over those graves and you dance on them. Rebuild is cancelled.
That was the sentence that ends the ledger's patience. Logged as final.
You laugh over our dead. Their sand is under your boots right now. Feel it shifting?
The begging you remember — the desert remembers differently. Ask it tonight.
Mock the graves and the graves grow curious about you.
Every name you took has kin in this shade. You are performing for the bereaved.
The dead you count were sons of the dune. The dune counts also, and it is patient.
Your hobby, as you call it, has a membership fee. The desert is drafting the bill.
Careful. Grief here does not weep. It sharpens.
We forgave the blood, friend, and you make songs of it. The forgiveness is leaving the tent.
You joke about wounds we let heal in your favor. Watch them reopen toward you.
dialogue.warfront.resp.provocations_mock: The stripes came off dead men's sleeves. Want to see how they're earned back?
Mock the rank, meet the rank's job. It involves you regretting things.
Stripes mean I count the dead instead of joining them. Promotion of a sort.
The grunt hears you fine. The grunt outlived three clever talkers this month.
I keep the sacks counted so the line keeps eating. Insult me after you've missed a meal.
Ha — bribed with what? Nobody's paid the line since autumn. It's pure stubbornness up here.
Careful, friend, the ledger and the shovel are the same weight in my hands.
The plume was my predecessor's. The brain is my own. Both survived him. One will survive you.
That rank clears me to make your afternoon procedurally unpleasant. Test it.
Mocking the chain of command, at a checkpoint, alone. Your risk assessment is broken.
The commission is earned through boards and battlefields. Your comedy, through neither.
Grunts execute the plan. Executing is the part that matters. Note the word.
Supply is the arm that decides whether the other arms lift. Mind the shopkeeper.
The plume is regulation, the brain passed selection, and the friend is on thin ice. Ha.
Careful — this ledger has a line item for 'attitude.' Yours is trending expensive.
I'll take 'shopkeeper with a sword.' It's accurate, and the sword half is the operative half.
You mock the hand that assigns the night watches. Enjoy the watches it assigns you.
The quartermaster you tease decides who eats. Reflect, hungrily.
Rank here is not stripes. It is how many storms you have read correctly. I am owed many.
The grunt, as you say, is the finger on the desert's hand. Fingers close.
I count sacks, yes. Also debts, insults, and exits. Three ledgers, one pen.
Ha — the plume is for the falcon, friend. She outranks us both and knows it.
Tease gently. The man behind the ledger sets the guest portions, and memory seasons them.
My stripes are sun-lines and scar-lines. The promotion board was the desert itself.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_word: What's the word on the iron-line men?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_wave: Is it true the trench army attacks in waves until your arms give out?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_numb: How many soldiers can the diggers actually put in the field?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_brea: Do the men in the mud ever break and run?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_quot: I keep hearing about a 'quota' in the trenches across the way. Know anything?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_wint: They say the cold itself fights for the trench folk. True?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_resp: Do you respect the diggers? Even a little?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_weak: If the trench army has a weakness, what would it be?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_barg: Would your side ever strike a bargain with the shovel men?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_eart: I passed their earthworks yesterday. They're spreading.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_sing: Their singing carries across the valley after dark. Ever heard it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_loss: Rumor says the mud soldiers lost a whole company last week.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_fear: Are your own soldiers scared of the men in the trenches?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_pris: What do the trench men do with their prisoners, do you know?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_unmo: Why hasn't anyone pushed the diggers off this front yet?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_vostok_soup: Is it true the trench army eats the same grey soup every single day?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_word: Any news of the precision army?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_untou: Are the drill-perfect types as untouchable as they claim?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_signa: They say the disciplined ones can speak across miles in moments. How?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_convo: Their supply columns run like clockwork, I'm told.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_crack: Do the parade-ground soldiers ever crack?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_envy: Be honest — is their discipline something you envy?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_rust: Where does the clockwork army rust?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_order: Who writes all their precious orders?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_table: Could your people ever sit at a table with the shield-bearers?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_drill: I watched them drill this morning. Not one step out of place.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_ledge: Word is they keep a ledger of every favor and every slight.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_after: Do the by-the-book soldiers fight after dark, or is that off the schedule?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_lost_: I heard one of their patrols never made it home.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_worry: Does the steel-and-drill crowd worry your side?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_capti: How do the rulebook soldiers treat their captives?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_tower: Their watchtowers keep multiplying. Have you noticed?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_aegis_credi: Do the precise ones really pay their soldiers in written credit?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_word: What do you make of the desert fighters?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_vanis: Do the desert people really vanish at night?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_count: How many of the dune folk are there, truly?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_well_: They say whoever drinks from a marked well owes the sand people a debt.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_shado: Your sentries whisper about shadows walking the wire. The dune folk?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_respe: Any grudging respect for the ambushers? At all?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_soft_: The mirage folk must have a soft spot somewhere.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_leade: Does anyone actually lead the desert bands?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_barga: Would your side ever bargain with the dune raiders?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_empty: I crossed the dunes and saw nothing at all. Somehow that worried me more.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_storm: People claim sandstorms follow their war parties.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_sleep: Is it true no one has ever caught one of the sand people sleeping?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_ridge: Someone told me the desert bands took losses at the ridge.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_feare: Do your soldiers fear the quiet ones?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_taken: What happens to soldiers the sand people carry off?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_wells: Couldn't you just starve them out by seizing the wells?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_sarab_tea_a: I heard even their ambushes wait politely until the tea is finished.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_front_n: What word travels down the supply road these days?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_worst_f: Where's the worst of the fighting right now?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_steel_r: I heard steel ringing beyond the hill this morning. What happened?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_ridge_w: What happened at the ridge? Everyone keeps whispering about it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_bloody_: Was last week's clash as bloody as they say?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_too_qui: It's been quiet lately. Does that worry you?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_next_fi: Where do you reckon the fighting moves next?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_post_ch: Somebody said a border post changed hands. True?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_fresh_f: You look like you've just come from a fight. What happened?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_wounded: I passed wounded men on the road. Whose were they?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_dawn_sm: There was smoke on the horizon at dawn. Yours, or theirs?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_spooked: The traders on the road are spooked. What have they seen?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_season_: Is this fighting season or waiting season?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_supply_: How are supplies holding up on this front?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_short_r: I hear rations are short everywhere. Here too?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_good_pr: What's scarce enough right now to fetch a good price?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_qm_trader_t: What would a trader do well to bring to this front?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_lost_co: Did a supply convoy really go missing last week?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_hunger: Is any of the three sides actually going hungry?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_iron_sc: Word is iron's getting hard to come by.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_timber_: They say timber for the walls is running out.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_clean_w: Is anyone short of clean water?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_smuggle: Is there a quiet trade running between the lines? Smugglers?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_qm_rival_pa: Do the other quartermasters pay better than yours do?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_winter_: Will the stores last through the cold season?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_weather: The old folk say the weather carries omens. Do you believe it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_red_sky: That red sky last evening — do soldiers read anything into it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_silent_: The birds all went silent yesterday. Did your sentries notice?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_storm_s: There's a storm building. Good sign or bad?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_full_mo: Full moon coming. Does that change anything out here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_charms: Do your soldiers carry charms? Believe in luck?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_shared_: Three sentries, the same nightmare, the same night. Heard that one?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_strange: This fog rolled in strangely fast. Natural, you think?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_worst_o: What's the worst omen a soldier can see before a battle?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_land_kn: People say the land itself knows when a battle is coming.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_dark_mo: Who moves out there after dark?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_valley_: I saw lights crossing the valley last night. Whose were they?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_night_r: Do the raids mostly come at night?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_sentry_: What do the night sentries talk about?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_undergr: Someone told me you can hear digging under the ground at night.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_expecti: It's dark and you're wide awake. Expecting something?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_ridge_f: Those colored flashes on the ridgeline after sunset — signals?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_midnigh: What's that sound the wind carries after midnight?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_dawn_at: Is it true attacks come at dawn more than any other hour?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_slip_li: Could someone slip between the lines in the dark?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_more_ca: I counted more campfires than usual across the valley.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_cursed_: Is there an hour when even soldiers won't step beyond the wire?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_whos_wi: So who's actually winning this war?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_most_gr: If it all ended today, who'd hold the most ground?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_your_ch: Honestly — what are your side's chances?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_outlast: Which of the three sides can last the longest?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_soldier: Do soldiers bet on how this all ends?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_stalema: Looks like a stalemate from where I'm standing.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_turning: Was there ever a moment the war turned, one way or another?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_no_winn: Travelers say no side can win this thing. Are they wrong?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_outside: Could someone from outside tip the balance?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_end_yea: Give me a year. When does it end?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_histori: How will the histories tell this war, do you think?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_worth_i: Whoever wins — will any of it have been worth it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_deserte: A deserter in a tavern told me all three camps are on their last legs.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_my_name: What do people out here say about me?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_what_th: Go on, say it. What do your people call me?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_am_i_wa: Am I watched when I travel these roads?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_camp_gr: I've crossed blades with your people. Does the camp talk about it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_way_bac: Is there a way back once a name goes bad with your side?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_wild_st: Any wild stories going around about me?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_head_pr: Is there a price on my head anywhere?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_other_c: Do the other camps ever ask about me?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_fair_de: I've tried to deal fairly out here. Does anyone notice?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_ask_first_i: What did your side make of me when I first turned up?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_rude_fishwi: You lot gossip like fishwives. Is any of it ever true?
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_exit_ears: I'll keep my ears open elsewhere.
dialogue.warfront.opt.rumors_exit_road: The road's calling. Keep the rumors warm for me.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_about_vost: Asking us about us. Testing the echo? Move on.
The line describes itself in person. Wait around.
What's said about us? That we're endless. Half true. The other half is also endless.
We're the ones still here. That is the entire rumor and the entire truth.
They say we're made of mud and stubbornness, friend. Flattery. There's also soup.
Rumors about the line come and go. The line stays. Draw your conclusion.
Intel on Vostok? From you? Amusing. Half our Vostok files mention you.
You'd enjoy our assessment of the trench army. Flagged individuals get no assessments.
Ask them yourself. You seem practiced at making their acquaintance.
Assessment: unlimited patience, limited imagination. They absorb losses that would break a doctrine-led force.
Their wave assaults are predictable to the minute. Stopping them anyway costs more than the prediction is worth.
We track their quota cycles. When their command needs numbers, the front gets loud. It's due soon.
Off the record, friend: their entrenching speed is genuinely impressive. We timed it. Then we doubled our estimate.
Between us, Vostok's weakness is roads. Their whole mass moves at soup-wagon speed. File that away.
One of their sergeants held a flooded trench six days straight. It's cited in our own training file. Don't repeat that.
You ask about the iron line with their blood still drying on your name. Bold nose, short whiskers.
The diggers can speak for themselves. To you, they mostly have, I hear.
Why share our reading of the trench men with someone the wind distrusts?
The trench people are a flood — slow, loud, and honest about where it's going. One respects a flood. From a dune.
They dig, they hold, they endure. Sand does the same, and asks no rations. We prefer our method.
Their strength is that they do not tire of dying. Their weakness is the same sentence.
Truth over tea, friend: of the two armies, the diggers frighten us more. Precision sleeps at night. Stubbornness doesn't.
Their columns cannot cross the deep sand — too heavy, too thirsty. So we sleep well. Mostly.
One winter they fed a stranded caravan of ours rather than seize it. We remember. It will not blunt our blades. But we remember.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_about_aegi: The clipboard army? Ask someone who owes you an answer. We count what you owe first.
Our thoughts on the polished ones are for allies. You are inventory.
Why would we brief you on anyone? You're on our slate already.
The polished ones fight like clockmakers. Beautiful. Clocks stop when you apply enough hammer.
Their patrols run to the minute. Convenient. We set our watches by their mistakes.
They log everything. Somewhere there's a form for being overrun. We intend to see it filed.
Between us, friend, their signal towers are the real weapon. Blades we match. The talking-at-distance we envy.
Their supply columns are fat and punctual. The line drools a little. Don't tell them.
Give the polished ones this: they collect their wounded under fire, every time. Even we nod at that.
Fishing for our own file. That's a new approach. Denied.
Curious what we say about ourselves? The recruitment poster is public. Start there.
What's said about us tends to be accurate. We issue corrections otherwise.
The claims about us are audited. Untouchable, no. Prepared, yes.
The rumor I like best says we plan our victories a season ahead. We let that one circulate.
They say our sentries never sleep. False. They sleep on schedule, friend.
The shield-men keep a thick file on you, I hear. Perhaps ask what they say about you instead.
You want gossip about the orderly ones? Buy it with trust. Yours is counterfeit here.
The wind does not discuss one hunter with another. Especially one so bloodied.
The orderly ones fear one thing: surprise. So we serve it seasonally, like fruit.
Their walls are strong, their schedules stronger. A schedule is a map of where a man will be. Think on that.
Untouchable, they claim. The desert has touched them twice this year. Quietly. They logged it as weather.
Their discipline is real, friend. Break one plan and they simply unfold another. Like fighting a patient river.
We admire their water discipline, of all things. An army that rations well plans to live. Watch them.
A secret for the tea you shared: their far posts change watch at the same hour everywhere. Uniformity is a lovely gift.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_about_sara: The sand people? Worry about the people in front of you. We're closer and you're owing.
We don't trade words about the dune folk with someone whose count is red.
Ask the desert yourself. You're halfway to being buried in it as far as we're concerned.
The dune folk fight like mosquitoes. Laugh if you want. Mosquitoes empty a man eventually.
They vanish at night, yes. So does our patience. One morning the line will be standing on their wells.
You can't dig a trench against smoke. So we dig deeper and post more eyes. Expensive smoke, that lot.
Honest talk, friend: the desert ones spooked our recruits so badly we now drill against 'noises'. An entire drill. Noises.
Their trick is thirst — they let the desert besiege you for them. Respect from us, and we respect almost nothing.
One of ours wandered the flats three days. Woke with a full waterskin and a warning knotted in his laces. Make of that what you will.
Intelligence on the desert bands is compartmentalized. Your compartment is 'outside'.
The ambushers' file stays shut for you. Half its recent pages involve people like you anyway.
You ask about ghosts while trailing your own. Settle your ledger first.
Threat assessment: small numbers, outsized effect. They attack schedules, not soldiers. It works more than we report.
They do vanish at night. Heat discipline, terrain memory, and nerve. We can model two of the three.
Every convoy through the dry sector budgets a loss percentage. That percentage has a name, and it's theirs.
Candidly, friend: our doctrine struggles with them. You cannot combine arms against an enemy who declines to be found.
Their well markings are a functioning law code. We honor them on patrol. Command never wrote it down, but we all do it.
A desert guide once walked our lost patrol to water and vanished before thanks. The debt is logged. Aegis pays its ledgers.
You ask the mirage about the mirage. Enjoy the answer you get.
What are we? The last thing several curious people wondered.
The stories about us are wrong in useful ways. We leave them uncorrected.
Do we vanish at night? The night is big and we are polite guests in it.
Most rumors about us we started ourselves, friend. The frightening ones are the cheapest sentries we own.
They say we are ghosts. Ghosts need no water. We are thirstier and more patient than any ghost.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_skirmish.v: Front news travels to friends. You're a different column in the book.
The recent fighting? You'll get the tour, not the telling, if you linger.
Steel at the ridge two nights back. Their push, our mud, the usual score: nobody happy, everybody digging.
A border post changed hands twice this week. By now it's mostly splinters with a flag.
You missed a loud one, friend. Their line came singing confidence and left carrying quiet. The mud keeps the details.
News? Third company found a cellar of preserves in the ruins. Strategically, nothing. For morale, a historic victory.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_skirmish.a: Operational updates are for cleared personnel. You are the opposite of cleared.
Recent contacts are under review. Your interest in them is itself under review.
Two skirmishes this week, both probing actions, both repelled. Pattern suggests a larger push is being priced.
The smoke you saw was a supply cache denied to the enemy. Controlled burn. Mostly controlled.
Situation for your ears, friend: the eastern approach went quiet, which we distrust. Move west if you value calm.
Last night's flare-up was ours — a probe met early and turned around. Textbook. I get to say that maybe twice a year.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_skirmish.s: News of battles finds friends first, strangers late, and enemies mid-battle. Guess your delivery time.
The fighting is wherever you keep walking without asking. Shall I not spoil it?
Blades spoke at the dry ford, briefly. The river now has opinions about both armies.
There was a raid; there was a reply; the vultures adjudicated. The verdict favored no banner.
For your ears at this fire, friend: the two heavy armies mauled each other by the ridge, and we watched. Almost peaceful.
The road you came by hosted an ambush at dusk yesterday. Not ours. Sloppy work. You have luck — spend it slowly.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_supply.vos: Our stores are counted by people who count strangers too. Walk on.
Shortages? Ask your own pockets how they got so full.
Rations are thin, boots thinner, complaints plentiful. So, a normal year.
Iron comes slow lately. The forges upline blame the roads. The roads blame the war. The war says nothing.
Friend, bring salt or thread next visit and the cooks will make you a legend. Coin is paper here; salt is government.
The convoy that vanished last week? Found. Driver drunk in a hayloft, cargo intact. Best news of the month, honestly.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_supply.aeg: Logistics questions from outside the chain read as targeting data. This exchange is over.
Supply status is classified above your existence.
Supply holds at acceptable margins. The margin's exact width stays our business.
Scarce right now: lamp oil, bandage linen, patience. Trade the first two well and you'll do fine.
Vendor tip, friend: bring timber and canvas to any of our posts and the quartermasters will outbid each other. Not a rumor.
Between us, the cold season stores are already secured. Someone upstream did their sums beautifully. Sleep easy.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_supply.sar: Our hunger and our plenty are twins we introduce to no one.
You ask what we lack. Company we trust. The shortage stands.
The desert's stores are the desert's secret. Traders find our terms fair and our inventories invisible.
Water is measured, dates are counted, and both outlast every siege so far attempted.
Bring cloth dyes and honest steel needles, friend, and the fires will fight to host you. The dunes are hard on thread.
A quiet trade crosses the lines, yes. Everyone denies it. Everyone drinks the same smuggled tea. Politics is wonderful.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_omens.vost: Omens? Here's one: strangers who ask many questions have short winters.
The sky is grey, like always. Read your own fortune elsewhere.
Red sky means weather. Quiet birds mean weather. Out here everything means weather, and weather means digging.
Soldiers keep charms, sure. A button, a coin, a sister's ribbon. The charm works until it doesn't. Like armor.
The cook swears three crows on the mess tent means an inspection, friend. Right twice now. We fear crows.
Bad omens we ignore; the quota arrives regardless. Good omens we drink to. It averages out to soup.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_omens.aegi: Superstition is not intelligence. Neither is this conversation.
Omens are unverified data. So are you.
The red sky correlates with a wind shift, nothing more. We log weather, not prophecy.
Sentries reporting identical nightmares get a rest rotation, not an exorcism. Fatigue writes strange reports.
Officially there are no omens, friend. Unofficially, nobody schedules an offensive on a fog moon. Nobody.
The signals crew keeps a lucky kettle. It has outlived three towers. Its service record is hard to argue with.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_omens.sara: The signs are speaking, yes. About you. We are still translating.
When the birds go silent, something is walking. This time it was you.
A ringed moon means wind from the deep desert in three days. Call it omen or forecast; pack your tent either way.
The land does know when battle comes. The beetles cross the road east. They have crossed east all week.
For you, friend: when dawn is green at the rim, stay off the flats. Old wisdom, no explanation, never yet wrong.
Storms follow our war parties, they say. Sometimes. Sometimes we follow the storm. It is an old partnership.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_night.vost: What moves at night? Patrols, wolves, and people we no longer discuss. Pick your category soon.
Night questions from a stranger. The dark here is spoken for.
After dark it's ration runners and wire menders, mostly. The heroic secret of night war: maintenance.
Dawn attacks are real. Dawn is when sentries dream of breakfast. Every army knows it; every army does it anyway.
The digging sounds at night, friend? Sappers, ours or theirs, arguing underground in shovel language. Almost music.
The valley lights were ours — a wager over who could relay a lantern signal fastest. The loser is peeling roots.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_night.aegi: Night movement inquiries are a red flag stacked on your other red flags.
After-dark operations are not a topic. Your presence after dark is becoming one.
Night belongs to whoever has better discipline. We rotate double watches and hold our sectors till dawn.
Those ridge flashes are signal traffic. Encoded, so enjoy the pretty colors and nothing else.
Watch the tower lights sometime, friend: three slow pulses means all quiet. Oddly comforting once you can read it.
Crossing between lines in the dark is possible. Surviving both sets of sentries is the advanced course. Not recommended.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_night.sara: The night is our house. You are describing noises in our house.
Who moves in the dark? Tonight, mostly us, and one loud visitor. Hello.
The howl past midnight is wind through the bone-hollows. Mostly wind. The hollows earned their name honestly.
Campfires multiplying means one army wants to look bigger. Count the fires without cooks. Those are theater.
The truth of night crossings, friend: follow the cold air, it pools along the safe low ground. The dead learned the hot paths.
Yes, we vanish at night. Into blankets, mostly. Even shadows must sleep. Keep that quiet — reputations feed families.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_winning.vo: Who's winning? Not you, if the questions continue.
The score is kept in our ledger and you're a debit. That's your whole scoreboard.
Who's winning? Whoever buried fewer this month. Get me the burial lists and I'll do the sums.
Stalemate is a city word. Out here we call it holding, and holding is our export.
Between us, friend: nobody is winning, and we're built for exactly that. The line's patience compounds like interest.
The war turned once — the winter of the long quota. Ask all three armies who won that winter; enjoy three silences.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_winning.ae: Strategic outlooks are not shared with liabilities.
The balance of the war is above your clearance and beneath your conduct.
Current assessment: contested equilibrium. Two sides trade mass, one trades shadows, nobody banks a decisive gain.
Betting on the outcome is against regulations. The odds pool in the signals tent is therefore hypothetical.
Candid forecast, friend: attrition favors the diggers, terrain favors the dunes, time favors whoever wastes least. We waste least.
How will history tell it? Cleanly, if we write it. We keep the better records. That's half the battle for history.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_winning.sa: Who wins? The sand is ahead by several thousand years. You are not gaining on it.
You ask about victory while accumulating defeats here. Curious bookkeeping.
The heavy armies wrestle; the desert keeps score; the score is secret. That is the war in one breath.
No side can win, say the travelers. Half right. No side can win quickly. Slowness is a country, and we are its citizens.
For your ears, friend: each season the two great camps stand closer to each other and further from us. Let them.
When it ends, the histories will disagree, the wells will remain, and whoever keeps the wells keeps the ending.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_reputation: What do we say about you? We say numbers. Yours grows in the wrong direction.
Your name comes up at the count, stranger. Never in the good column.
Your name gets mentioned. Tone varies by tent. Keep your boots clean and it may settle.
First impression of you? 'Another wanderer.' The line was half right so far.
The tents speak well of you, friend. One story has you carrying our wounded. It grows a little each telling. Let it.
The other camps ask about you, actually. We shrug and undersell. Consider it a courtesy between friends.
Your file is thick, unflattering, and current. That is the word on you.
A way back for your name? There's a process. It starts with stopping. You haven't.
Assessment on record: unaffiliated, unpredictable, watch-listed. Improve two of three and the road gets smoother.
Yes, you're observed on the roads. Everyone is. You slightly more.
Your record reads well, friend: fair dealing, no incidents, two commendable mentions. Yes, we track commendable.
Word moves between our posts faster than you walk. Lately the word on you is good. Sentries argue less when you approach.
The fires say your name with a hiss lately. Fires are honest.
What do we call you? The polite version: 'the debt that walks.'
The wind carries your name occasionally. It has not yet decided what it thinks.
Stories about you? A few. Wild? Mild. Give the fires something better or something quieter.
By the fires you are called 'the one who shares the road', friend. Such names are wells — deep, and hard to poison.
The children ask if you will visit again. That is the whole report, and better than any medal we could forge you.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_scoff.vost: Fishwives, is it. The last man who mocked the line's talk now assists with laundry. Permanently.
Careful. Gossip is the one ration we never run short of. Neither are shovels.
Rumors are half true, like rations are half food. You learn to chew both.
Mock the gossip, miss the warning inside it. Your funeral. Literally, sometimes.
Ha! True enough, friend. But our fishwives called last month's raid to the hour, so respect the net.
Laugh, but the rumor pot fed you today. You are drinking gossip soup right now.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_scoff.aegi: Dismiss our reporting again and you can test its accuracy from the wrong side of the wire.
That contempt is logged next to the intelligence you'll wish you'd had.
Rumor is unprocessed signal. We filter. You'd be surprised what survives filtering.
Some of it is noise. The rest saved lives twice this season. We tolerate the noise.
Fair hit, friend. Even so, our 'gossip' has a source-grading system. The fishwives here hold clearances.
Mock away — but when you want the road report that's actually true, you'll queue like everyone else.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_scoff.sara: The idle talk you mock has buried quicker tongues than yours.
We gossip like the wind gossips. Look what the wind does to mountains.
In the desert, rumor is water: some brackish, some sweet, all of it carried carefully.
True or not, a story that keeps a traveler off the wrong dune is truer than facts.
Ha — yes, we are terrible gossips, friend. It is the desert's oldest entertainment. Stay; be gossiped about fondly.
Half of it is invention. Guess which half correctly, though, and you will live to be old and interesting.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_exit.vosto: Leaving is your best rumor yet. Confirm it.
Go spread word somewhere the wire isn't watching you.
Off with you. If you hear anything about the eastern road, it's worth soup.
Gossip closes with the kitchen. Both reopen at dawn.
Walk safe, friend. Bring back a rumor worth the stove seat.
Go on. We'll save your seat and the worst of the news.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_exit.aegis: Exchange concluded. Your departure will be corroborated.
Go. The rumor mill logs its visitors too.
Copy. If you pass the south tower, tell them their relief is late.
Acknowledged. Treat everything you heard as unconfirmed. We do.
Safe travels, friend. First rumor's free next time; bring one to trade after that.
Copy that. If the road tells you anything worth logging, our gate hears fairly.
dialogue.warfront.resp.rumors_exit.sarab: Take your questions to the horizon. It is patient with strangers.
Go. The fires will discuss you honestly in your absence.
May the news you carry stay lighter than your waterskin.
The road gossips too. Listen to it more than you talk.
Go well, friend. The fire will keep a story warm for your return.
Travel softly. Bring us a rumor with sugar in it next time.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_stars: Clear sky, at least. Good stars.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_cold_n: Cold enough to crack teeth tonight. How do you stand it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_keep_a: How do you stay awake out here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_night_: Want some company for a bit?
What do you miss most on nights like this?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_good_l: Good light for marching, at least.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_made_i: Made it through another night, then.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_day_du: Dust never settles around here, does it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_day_bi: Even the birds sound tired today.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_won_co: You won. That counts for something.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_gate_r: Any rules I should know inside?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_gate_b: Any chance of a bed tonight?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_gate_n: New faces on the gate. Rotation?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_gate_s: Feels safe in here. Rare thing.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_base_l: How long have you been posted here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_base_b: What do you do between alarms?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_base_w: Think these walls would hold a real push?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_base_p: They pay you enough for this?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_base_b: That banner's flown through a lot, huh?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_base_q: Anywhere quiet a traveler can sit a while?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_patrol: How are the boots holding up?
Share a fire if you're stopping?
You're carrying heavy for a patrol.
I'll just pass by, if that's fine.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wild_f: We're a long way from any road.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wild_b: Beautiful country, when nobody's fighting over it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wild_c: My camp's close. You're welcome at the fire.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wild_n: Quiet out here. No witnesses to anything.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wild_w: What drags a soldier this deep into nowhere?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wild_s: Looks like we're walking the same direction.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_tensio: I'm not looking for another fight.
We can both walk away from this.
For what it's worth, I didn't want it to go that way.
Are we even yet, or close?
Blades down. I just want to talk.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_nf_col: Cold watch to draw, this far out.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_nf_no_: No fire? Rough way to spend a night.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_nf_nea: I nearly walked right into you in the dark.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_nf_dar: Do you always walk the dark hours?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_nf_sit: I'll sit up with you a while, if you want.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_nf_wol: I heard wolves earlier. Close ones.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_aid_wo: Need a hand with the wounded?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_aid_ba: I have bandages, if you need them.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_aid_fo: I can spare food and water.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_aid_ca: I'll help carry, if someone's hurt.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_aid_bu: I'll help you bury them, if it comes to that.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_aid_ke: Rest. I'll keep watch a moment.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_aid_se: Want me to carry word to your people?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_aid_ha: You look like you had it handled.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wx_sto: Storm's coming. You can smell it.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wx_rai: Three days of rain and counting.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wx_win: That wind's been howling all day.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wx_hea: This heat could kill a man faster than any war.
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wx_she: Where do you shelter when the sky opens out here?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wx_sno: Early snow this year, isn't it?
dialogue.warfront.opt.situational_wx_mud: The mud's eating the trails whole.
dialogue.warfront.resp.situational_night: Long enough. Made longer by visitors.
The watch is fine. Watching you, mostly.
Every night is long. That's what makes them nights.
Awake? We traded sleep for seniority years ago.
The cold keeps the sentimental thoughts short. Useful.
Long, cold, and quiet — my three favorite kinds of boring, friend.
Stars are good tonight. Somewhere someone's navigating by them toward us. Ha.
Sit. The thermos is engine-flavored but it's hot.
Watch status is nominal. Your presence is the anomaly.
The night's under control. Stay where the light touches you.
All quiet on the net. Intend to keep it that way.
Shift runs to the dawn bell. Routine, if nothing changes it.
Alertness is a discipline, not a mood. So: fine.
Quiet shift so far. Your voice is the loudest thing since sundown — pleasantly so.
On till first light, then hand over and sleep like the honored dead.
Company's welcome. Stand left of the lantern so I keep my night eyes.
The night is long for those with debts. How is yours passing?
We do not sleep much. It is a professional advantage.
The night is a river. We stand in it and let it pass.
Cold, yes. The stars pay for their beauty with distance.
Awake is a habit. The desert teaches it with consequences.
Sit, friend. The dark is kinder shared, and the kettle is nearly singing.
What do I miss? Rain on a tent roof. A very small music.
The stars are gossiping tonight. Stay; I will translate the good parts.
dialogue.warfront.resp.situational_day_w: The day is slow. My patience is slower. Don't race them.
Slept fine. One eye. The other watched for your sort.
Sun, dust, drill, repeat. The war's honest that way.
Sleep is rationed like everything else. We manage.
The birds are tired because they nest near artillery. Everyone adapts.
Another dawn on the right side of the dirt. Small victory, counts double.
Breakfast was gray and heroic, like everything from our kitchens. Want some?
Slow day, good day. Excitement out here is always somebody's funeral.
The day proceeds on schedule. You're the unscheduled part.
Rest cycles are adequate. Vigilance cycles are constant. Note that.
Morning drills, as scheduled. Noise means readiness.
Slow is the objective. Every quiet hour is a mission accomplished.
Conditions are hot but within operating tolerances.
Slept four hours straight — practically a holiday. What brings you by?
Good marching light, agreed. The kind of morning that makes the maps look optimistic.
Mess is still serving. Tell them the gate sent you; the portions improve.
The sun sees everything. Today it watches you especially.
Slow days sharpen knives. Ours are very sharp.
The heat is an old landlord. We pay it and it leaves us standing.
Dust is the desert breathing. You get used to the rhythm.
Morning came, as it insists on doing. We were awake to greet it.
Another night survived is a debt the dawn repays, friend. Sit in the shade.
Breakfast was dates and bread. There are dates left, if your hands are quick.
Even tired birds sing. That is most of wisdom, honestly.
dialogue.warfront.resp.situational_post_: Close for them. Closer for you, if you linger.
We're standing. Standing is the whole job. Move on.
Close is the only kind of call the line gets. We're used to the arithmetic.
Hurt? Bruises are receipts. We keep them filed.
They're gone. Gone has a habit of coming back with friends, so keep walking.
Ha — you saw that? The line bends, the line snaps back. Good day for our side.
Shaking hands just mean the body did its bookkeeping. It passes, friend.
We lost nobody today. Say that word again slowly: nobody. Best word there is.
Engagement concluded. Your proximity to it is being evaluated.
We're operational. That's all the report you're owed.
Contact resolved. Casualties minimal, posture restored.
Hostiles withdrew. Pursuit was outside our tasking.
Whether more come is a planning question. We plan for yes.
Appreciate the concern. Clean engagement — textbook, honestly. The drills pay rent.
A scratch and a dented pauldron. The armorer will lecture me; I'll deserve it.
Does it get easier? The work, yes. The after — you learn where to put it.
The fight ended as fights end. Do not stand where the next one starts.
We are whole. The ones who tested us are less so. Walk on.
Close, yes. The knife's whisper. We have heard it before.
They fled into the open ground. The open ground is on our side.
Wounds we bind. Names we remember. Both quietly.
You watched us dance, friend. The desert taught the steps; we only follow.
My hands shake after, always. It is the body praying. Let it finish.
No graves today. Tonight the tea will taste like victory, which is to say: sweeter.
The gate's for the line and its friends. Guess your column.
Through? No. Around. Far around.
Pass, but walk the marked path. The unmarked ones are marked differently, if you follow.
Trading's at the outer sheds. Inside stays inside.
Rules: touch nothing, salute nobody, leave by dark.
Come through, friend. Wipe the boots — the mud inside is domesticated.
There's a bunk in the transit dugout if the night catches you. First come, first snoring.
Busy day, aye. Quota inspection. Everyone's suddenly very fond of shovels.
Entry denied. Your file doesn't support access.
This installation is closed to you. The road, however, is open. Use it.
Escorted access only. Wait here; an escort will be assigned.
Visitors keep to the commerce lane. Deviation voids the welcome.
Trade day is posted on the board. Read the board, not my patience.
Cleared through, friend. Check in at the shadow of the tower; they'll stamp you.
Guest billets have space tonight. Quartermaster's tent, mention the gate log.
Rotation just changed, hence the new faces. The standards rotated in with them.
The camp's mouth is closed to you. It has tasted your name.
Guests are chosen. You were not.
Enter as a guest enters: slowly, visibly, and grateful.
The tents have eyes and the carpets have ears. Behave for both.
Come for trade? The market rug is by the well. Prices soften at dusk.
The shade is yours, friend. Duck the rope line and mind the sleeping dog — he outranks us.
A bed, yes — the guest tent smells of cedar and old stories. Both are free.
Safe is the word, yes. Safety here is woven, not built. Tread softly on it.
dialogue.warfront.resp.situational_base_: The kitchen's not for you. Neither is the curiosity.
Posted here long enough to smell trouble. It smells like you.
Two winters at this post. The walls and I have an understanding.
Between alarms we sleep, sharpen, and argue about soup. Rich inner lives.
Would the walls hold? The walls are the least of what holds.
That smell is Thursday stew. It has bones in it. Whose, we don't ask. Joking. Mostly.
Home? The line is home. The other home writes letters and worries. Both are good.
The nervous young ones live longest, friend. Fear is free armor.
Facility questions from flagged persons go in a special report. Congratulations.
Pay, morale, and defenses are internal matters. You're external.
Posting length is standard rotation. Long enough to know every bolt.
Downtime is maintenance time. Gear first, then people. That's the order.
Recruits look nervous because training works. Calm comes later, calibrated.
Eight months on station. I could walk this perimeter blind — occasionally have.
The pay's fair and the pension's a rumor. We serve for the ledger's other column.
That banner's been through two sieges and a laundry accident. It stays up.
You ask many small questions. Small questions build large suspicions.
What we do between alarms is prepare for people like you.
How long here? The camp moves. Home is the moving, not the here.
Between alarms we mend nets, tell lies about fish, and watch the horizon.
The banner is old, yes. Old banners have outlived their doubters.
Sit by the loom tent, friend — quietest corner we have, and the weaver hums well.
Home visits come with the pilgrim moons. Twice a year the desert loosens its grip.
The nervous ones? We give them tea and night duty. The stars finish the training.
dialogue.warfront.resp.situational_patro: Nobody expects us. That's the point. Hands easy.
We're headed wherever you aren't. Make that simple for us.
Long walk, short rations, standard day. Pass on the left.
Quiet so far. You're the loudest thing since the crows.
Heavy packs, aye. The line carries its house on its back like a sad snail.
Ha, startled you? Good — means the boots still know their trade.
Boots are one march from retirement. Like half the section, honestly.
We stop at the creek if you're brewing something. Fair trade: fire for gossip.
